title: Self-adaptation of Genetic Operators Through Genetic Programming Techniques Conference: GECCO ’17; July 15-19, 2017; Berlin, Germany Price: 15.00 DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.1145/3071178.3071214 ISBN: 978-1-4503-4920-8/17/07 CCS: Theory of computation Bio-inspired optimization CCS: Theory of computati
creator: Andres Felipe Cruz-Salinas, Jonatan Gomez Perdomo
description: Abstract . Here we propose an evolutionary algorithm that self modifies its operators at the same time that candidate solutions are evolved. This tackles convergence and lack of diversity issues, leading to better solutions. Operators are represented as trees and are evolved using genetic programming (GP) techniques.

title: Radiative Seesaw Model and DAMPE Excess from Leptophilic Gauge Symmetry
creator: Zhi-Long Han 1, Weijian Wang 2, Ran Ding 3
description: Abstract In the light of the e + + e − e^{+}+e^{-} excess observed by DAMPE experiment, we propose an anomaly-free radiative seesaw model with an alternative leptophilic U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} gauge symmetry. In the model, only right-handed leptons are charged under U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} symmetry.

title: On non-normality and classification of amplification mechanisms in stability and resolvent analysis
creator: Sean Symon, Kevin Rosenberg, Scott T. M. Dawson, Beverley J. McKeon
description: Abstract We seek to quantify non-normality of the most amplified resolvent modes and predict their features based on the characteristics of the base or mean velocity profile. A 2-by-2 model linear Navier-Stokes (LNS) operator illustrates how non-normality from mean shear distributes perturbation energy in different velocity components of the forcing and response modes.

title: Language and Noise Transfer in Speech Enhancement Generative Adversarial Network
creator: Santiago Pascual, Maruchan Park, Joan Serrà, Antonio Bonafonte, Kang-Hun Ahn
description: Abstract Speech enhancement deep learning systems usually require large amounts of training data to operate in broad conditions or real applications. This makes the adaptability of those systems into new, low resource environments an important topic. In this work, we present the results of adapting a speech enhancement generative adversarial network by fine-tuning the generator with small amounts of data.

title: Properties of Two-Temperature Dissipative Accretion Flow Around Black Holes 2016 Properties of Two-Temperature Dissipative Accretion Flow Around Black Holes – References
creator: Indu K. Dihingia, Santabrata Das, Samir Mandal
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Indu K. Dihingia, Santabrata Das, Samir Mandal. We study the properties of two-temperature accretion flow around a non-rotating black hole in presence of various dissipative processes where pseudo-Newtonian potential is adopted to mimic the effect of general relativity. The flow encounters energy loss by means of radiative processes acted on the electrons and at the same time, flow heats up as a consequence of viscous heating effective on ions.

title: Near-Exact Non-relativistic Ionisation Energies for Many-Electron Atoms
creator: E. O. Jobunga
description: Abstract Electron-electron interactions and correlations form the basis of difficulties encountered in the theoretical solution of problems dealing with multi-electron systems. Accurate treatment of the electron-electron problem is likely to unravel some nice physical properties of matter embedded in the interaction.

title: Constraints on jet quenching in p–Pb collisions at 𝒔 𝐍𝐍 = 5.02 \bm{\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}}=5.02 TeV measured by the event-activity dependence of semi-inclusive hadron-jet distributions See Appendix A for the list of collaboration members
description: Abstract The ALICE Collaboration reports the measurement of semi-inclusive distributions of charged-particle jets recoiling from a high-transverse momentum trigger hadron in p–Pb collisions at s NN = 5.02 \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02 TeV. Jets are reconstructed from charged-particle tracks using the anti- k T k_{\mathrm{T}} algorithm with resolution parameter R = 0.2 R=0.2 and 0.4.

title: Search for the \cmsSymbolFace ​ X ​ ( 5568 ) \cmsSymbolFace{X}(5568) state decaying into \PBzs ​ \Pgppm \PBzs\Pgppm in proton-proton collisions at s = 8 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=8\TeV
description: Abstract A search for resonance-like structures in the \PBzs ​ \Pgppm \PBzs\Pgppm invariant mass spectrum is performed using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC at s = 8 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=8\TeV , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 19.7 \fbinv .

title: MEBoost: Mixing Estimators with Boosting for Imbalanced Data Classification
creator: Farshid Rayhan, Sajid Ahmed, Asif Mahbub, Md. Rafsan Jani, Swakkhar Shatabda, Dewan Md. Farid and Chowdhury Mofizur Rahman
description: Abstract Class imbalance problem has been a challenging research problem in the fields of machine learning and data mining as most real life datasets are imbalanced. Several existing machine learning algorithms try to maximize the accuracy classification by correctly identifying majority class samples while ignoring the minority class.

title: DecideNet: Counting Varying Density Crowds Through Attention Guided Detection and Density Estimation
creator: Jiang Liu, Chenqiang Gao, Deyu Meng, Alexander G. Hauptmann
description: Abstract In real-world crowd counting applications, the crowd densities vary greatly in spatial and temporal domains. A detection based counting method will estimate crowds accurately in low density scenes, while its reliability in congested areas is downgraded. A regression based approach, on the other hand, captures the general density information in crowded regions.

title: Theoretical Analysis of Inducer and Operator Binding for Cyclic-AMP Receptor Protein Mutants
creator: Tal Einav
description: Abstract Abstract Allosteric transcription factors undergo binding events both at their inducer binding sites as well as at distinct DNA binding domains, and it is often difficult to disentangle the structural and functional consequences of these two classes of interactions.

title: Mining Smart Card Data for Travelers’ Mini Activities
creator: Boris Chidlovskii
description: Abstract In the context of public transport modeling and simulation, we address the problem of mismatch between simulated transit trips and observed ones. We point to the weakness of the current travel demand modeling process; the trips it generates are over-optimistic and do not reflect the real passenger choices.

title: A topological interpretation of three Leibnizian Principles within the Functional Extensions Thanks: It is a great pleasure to dedicate this paper to Furio: how many joint papers in the Eighties and Nineties deal with mathematical structures arising from fundamental philosophical principles!
creator: Marco Forti
description: Abstract . Three philosophical principles are often quoted in connection with Leibniz: “objects sharing the same properties are the same object” ( Identity of indiscernibles ), “everything can possibly exist, unless it yields contradiction” ( Possibility as consistency ), and “the ideal elements correctly determine the real things” ( Transfer ).

title: Un scindage du morphisme de Frobenius sur l’algèbre des distributions d’un groupe réductif
creator: Michel Gros, K aneda Masaharu
description: Abstract Pour un groupe algébrique semi-simple simplement connexe sur un corps algébriquement clos de caractéristique positive, nous avons précédemment construit un scindage de l’endomorphisme de Frobenius sur son algèbre des distributions. Nous généralisons la construction au cas de des groupes réductifs et en dégageons les corollaires correspondants.

title: DESY 17-197 Probing light top partners with CP violation
creator: Giuliano Panico, Marc Riembau, Thibaud Vantalon, [10mm] IFAE, BIST, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, E-08193 Bellaterra, Barcelona, Spain
description: Abstract We investigate CP-violating effects induced by light top partners in composite Higgs theories. We find that sizable contributions to the dipole moments of the light SM quarks and leptons are generically generated at the two-loop level through Barr–Zee-type diagrams.

title: TIME-DEPENDENT ELECTRON ACCELERATION IN PULSAR WIND TERMINATION SHOCKS: APPLICATION TO THE 2011 APRIL CRAB NEBULA GAMMA-RAY FLARE
creator: John J. Kroon, Peter A. Becker, Justin D. Finke
description: Abstract The γ \gamma -ray flares from the Crab nebula observed by AGILE and Fermi -LAT between 2007-2013 reached GeV photon energies and lasted several days. The strongest emission, observed during the 2011 April “super-flare,” exceeded the quiescent level by more than an order of magnitude.

title: A Roadmap for HEP Software and Computing R&D for the 2020s
creator: HEP Software Foundation
description: Abstract Particle physics has an ambitious and broad experimental programme for the coming decades. This programme requires large investments in detector hardware, either to build new facilities and experiments, or to upgrade existing ones. Similarly, it requires commensurate investment in the R&D of software to acquire, manage, process, and analyse the shear amounts of data to be recorded.

title: Online Submodular Welfare Maximization: Greedy Beats 1 2 \frac{1}{2} in Random Order Thanks: An extended abstract of this paper appeared at ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC)’ 2015.
creator: Nitish Korula, Vahab Mirrokni, Morteza Zadimoghaddam
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Nitish Korula, Vahab Mirrokni, Morteza Zadimoghaddam. In the Submodular Welfare Maximization (SWM) problem, the input consists of a set of n n items, each of which must be allocated to one of m m agents. Each agent ℓ \ell has a valuation function v ℓ v_{\ell} , where v ℓ ​ ( S ) v_{\ell}(S) denotes the welfare obtained by this agent if she receives the set of items S S .

title: Status of MERLIN
creator: H. Rafique 1 ​ 2 ​ 3 {}^{1~2~3}, R. B. Appleby 2 ​ 3 {}^{2~3}, R. J. Barlow 1, J. G. Molson 5, S. Tygier 2 ​ 3 {}^{2~3}, A. Valloni 2 ​ 4 {}^{2~4}
description: Abstract MERLIN is an accelerator physics library written in C++ which can be used for a range of accelerator tracking simulations, including collimation in hadron colliders. Recently MERLIN has been upgraded to provide a robust tool for HL-LHC collimation, including the treatment of composite materials, and a hollow electron lens process.

title: The one-dimensional asymmetric persistent random walk
creator: Vincent Rossetto
description: Abstract Persistent random walks are intermediate transport processes between a uniform rectilinear motion and a Brownian motion. They are formed by successive steps of random finite lengths and directions travelled at a fixed speed. The isotropic and symmetric one-dimensional persistent random walk is governed by the telegrapher’s equation, also called hyperbolic heat conduction equation.

title: Experimental entanglement of temporal order
creator: Giulia Rubino, Lee A. Rozema, Francesco Massa, Mateus Araújo, Magdalena Zych, Časlav Brukner, Philip Walther
description: Abstract The study of causal relations has recently been applied to the quantum realm, leading to the discovery that not all physical processes have a definite causal structure. While indefinite causal processes have previously been experimentally shown, these proofs relied on the quantum description of the experiments.

title: Wave propagation through an elastically-asymmetric architected material
creator: Vladislav A. Yastrebov
description: Abstract A one-dimensional wave propagation through elastically asymmetric media is investigated. A class of metamaterials possessing an arbitrary elastic asymmetry is proposed. This asymmetry results in different wave speeds of tensile and compressive components of elastic waves. The faster component can overtake the slower one resulting in their dissipative annihilation through energy cascades.

title: Joint model-based recognition and localization of overlapped acoustic events using a set of distributed small microphone arrays
creator: Rupayan Chakraborty, Climent Nadeu
description: Abstract In the analysis of acoustic scenes, often the occurring sounds have to be detected in time, recognized, and localized in space. Usually, each of these tasks is done separately. In this paper, a model-based approach to jointly carry them out for the case of multiple simultaneous sources is presented and tested.

title: Quadrilateral grid generation supported on complex internal boundaries using spectral methods Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
creator: Saúl E. Buitrago Boret, Oswaldo J. Jiménez P
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Saúl E. Buitrago Boret, Oswaldo J. Jiménez P. This work concerns with the following problem. Given a two-dimensional domain whose boundary is a closed polygonal line with internal boundaries defined also by polygonal lines, it is required to generate a grid consisting only of quadrilaterals with the following features: (1) conformal, that is, to be a tessellation of the two-dimensional domain such that the intersection of any two quadrilaterals is a vertex, an edge or empty (never a portion of one edge), (2) structured,

title: Quantum Abelian Yang–Mills Theory on Riemannian Manifolds with Boundary
creator: Homero G. DÍAZ-MARÍN † and Robert OECKL ‡
description: Abstract We quantize abelian Yang–Mills theory on Riemannian manifolds with boundaries in any dimension. The quantization proceeds in two steps. First, the classical theory is encoded into an axiomatic form describing solution spaces associated to manifolds. Second, the quantum theory is constructed from the classical axiomatic data in a functorial manner.

title: Comment on “Probing gravitational wave polarizations with signals from compact binary coalescences”
creator: Anatoly A. Svidzinsky
description: Abstract In a recent paper “Probing gravitational wave polarizations with signals from compact binary coalescences” (arXiv:1710.03794 [gr-qc]) the authors argue that a single detection of gravitational wave by the LIGO-Virgo network is capable to distinguish between pure tensor and pure vector polarizations of gravitational waves.

title: Flat affine subvarieties in Oeljeklaus-Toma manifolds
creator: Liviu Ornea
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Liviu Ornea. Abstract: The Oeljeklaus-Toma (OT-) manifolds are compact, complex, non-Kähler manifolds constructed by Oeljeklaus and Toma, and generalizing the Inoue surfaces. Their construction uses the number-theoretic data: a number field K and a torsion-free subgroup U in the group of units of the ring of integers of K , with rank of U equal to the number of real embeddings of K .

title: Optimising matrix product state simulations of Shor’s algorithm
creator: Aidan Dang, Charles D. Hill, Lloyd C. L. Hollenberg
description: Abstract We detail techniques to optimise high-level classical simulations of Shor’s quantum factoring algorithm. Chief among these is to examine the entangling properties of the circuit and to effectively map it across the one-dimensional structure of a matrix product state.

title: Coherent control theory and experiment of optical phonons in diamond
creator: Hiroya Sasaki, Riho Tanaka, Yasuaki Okano, Fujio Minami, Yosuke Kayanuma, Yutaka Shikano, Kazutaka G. Nakamura
description: Abstract The coherent control of optical phonons has been experimentally demonstrated in various physical systems. While the transient dynamics for optical phonons can be explained by phenomenological models, the coherent control experiment cannot be explained due to the quantum interference.

title: Differential calculus over double Lie algebroids
creator: Sophie Chemla
description: Abstract . M. Van den Bergh ( [ 18 ] ) defined the notion of a double Lie algebroid and showed that a double quasi-Poisson algebra gives rise to a double Lie algebroid. We give new examples of double Lie algebroids and develop a differential calculus in that context.

title: Studying Pulsed Laser Deposition conditions for Ni/C-based multi-layers
creator: Tjeerd R.J. Bollmann
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Tjeerd R.J. Bollmann. Nickel carbon based multi-layers are a viable route towards future hard X-ray and soft γ \gamma -ray focusing telescopes. Here, we study the Pulsed Laser Deposition growth conditions of such bilayers by Reflective High Energy Electron Diffraction, X-ray Reflectivity and Diffraction, Atomic Force Microscopy, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy and cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy analysis, with emphasis on optimization of process pressure and substrate temperature during growth.

title: Experimental Demonstration of Quantum Tunneling in IBM Quantum Computer
creator: Narendra N. Hegade, Nachiket L. Kortikar, Bikramaditya Das, Bikash K. Behera, Prasanta K. Panigrahi
description: Abstract Quantum computers are the promising candidates for simulation of large quantum systems, which is a daunting task to perform in a classical computer. Here, we report the experimental realization of quantum tunneling of a single particle through different types of potential barriers by performing digital quantum simulations using IBM quantum computers.

title: On P P -unique hypergraphs
creator: J.A. Makowsky
description: Abstract We study hypergraphs which are uniquely determined by their chromatic, independence and matching polynomials. B. Bollobás, L. Pebody and O. Riordan (2000) conjectured (BPR-conjecture) that almost all graphs are uniquely determined by their chromatic polynomials. We show that for r r -uniform hypergraphs with r ≥ 3 r\geq 3 this is almost never the case.

title: Search for lepton flavour violating decays of the Higgs boson to μ ​ τ \mu\tau and \Pe ​ τ \Pe\tau in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: Abstract A search for lepton flavour violating decays of the Higgs boson in the μ ​ τ \mu\tau and \Pe ​ τ \Pe\tau decay modes is presented. The search is based on a data set corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.

title: The cavity approach for Steiner trees packing Problems
creator: Alfredo Braunstein, Anna Paola Muntoni
description: Abstract The Belief Propagation approximation, or cavity method, has been recently applied to several combinatorial optimization problems in its zero-temperature implementation, the max-sum algorithm. In particular, recent developments to solve the edge-disjoint paths problem and the prize-collecting Steiner tree problem on graphs have shown remarkable results for several classes of graphs and for benchmark instances.

title: Bose–Einstein correlations in \Pp ​ \Pp \Pp\Pp , \Pp \Pp Pb, and PbPb collisions at s NN = \sqrt{\smash[b]{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}}= 0.9–7 \TeV
description: Abstract Quantum statistical (Bose–Einstein) two-particle correlations are measured in pp collisions at s = 0.9 \sqrt{s}=0.9 , 2.76, and 7 \TeV , as well as in \Pp \Pp Pb and peripheral PbPb collisions at nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energies of 5.02 and 2.76 \TeV , respectively, using the CMS detector at the LHC.

title: Equivalence of tensor products over a category of W ∗ -algebras
description: Abstract We prove the equivalence of two tensor products over a category of W ∗ -algebras with normal (not necessarily unital) ∗ -homomorphisms, defined by Guichardet and Dauns, respectively. This structure differs from the standard tensor product construction by Misonou–Takeda–Turumaru, which is based on weak topological completion, and does not have a categorical universality property.

title: Identification of heavy-flavour jets with the CMS detector in pp collisions at 13 \TeV
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by . Many measurements and searches for physics beyond the standard model at the LHC rely on the efficient identification of heavy-flavour jets, \ie jets originating from bottom or charm quarks. In this paper, the discriminating variables and the algorithms used for heavy-flavour jet identification during the first years of operation of the CMS experiment in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV , are presented.

title: Constant Approximation Algorithms for Guarding Simple Polygons using Vertex Guards
creator: Pritam Bhattacharya, Subir Kumar Ghosh, Sudebkumar Prasant Pal
description: Abstract The art gallery problem enquires about the least number of guards sufficient to ensure that an art gallery, represented by a simple polygon P P , is fully guarded. Most standard versions of this problem are known to be NP-hard.

title: Honors Thesis: On the faithfulness of the Burau representation at roots of unity Thanks: A great deal of thanks to my advisors on this project, A. Parker from Wittenberg University and B. Winarski from University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, for their help and guidance. You were both instrumental in the
creator: Thomas Chuna
description: Abstract . We study the kernel of the evaluated Burau representation through the braid element σ 1 ​ σ 2 ​ σ 1 \sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}\sigma_{1} . This element is significant as a part of the standard braid relation. We establish the form of this element’s image raised to the k t ​ h k^{th} power.

title: Echo-Ramsey Interferometry with Motional Quantum States
creator: D. Hu, L. X. Niu, S. J. Jin, X. Z. Chen, G. J. Dong, J. Schmiedmayer, X. J. Zhou
description: Abstract Ramsey interferometers (RIs) using internal electronic or nuclear states find wide applications in science and engineering. We develop a matter wave Ramsey interferometer for motional quantum states exploiting the S- and D-bands of an optical lattice and identify the different de-phasing and de-coherence mechanisms. We implement a band echo technique, employing repeated π \pi -pulses.

title: The equation of state of a cell fluid model in the supercritical region
creator: M.P. Kozlovskii, I.V. Pylyuk, O.A. Dobush
description: Abstract The analytic method for deriving the equation of state of a cell fluid model in the region above the critical temperature ( T ⩾ T c T\geqslant T_{\text{c}} ) is elaborated using the renormalization group transformation in the collective variables set.

title: Mixin Composition Synthesis based on Intersection Types Thanks: This work was partially supported by EU COST Action IC1201: BETTY and MIUR PRIN CINA Prot. 2010LHT4KM, San Paolo Project SALT. Tzu-chun Chen is also partially supported by the ERC grant FP7-617805 LiVeSoft – Lightweight Verification of
creator: Jan Bessai \rsuper a, Tzu-Chun Chen \rsuper b, Andrej Dudenhefner \rsuper a, Boris Düdder \rsuper a, Ugo de’Liguoro \rsuper c, Jakob Rehof \rsuper a
description: Abstract . We present a method for synthesizing compositions of mixins using type inhabitation in intersection types. First, recursively defined classes and mixins, which are functions over classes, are expressed as terms in a lambda calculus with records. Intersection types with records and record-merge are used to assign meaningful types to these terms without resorting to recursive types.

title: Search for heavy resonances decaying into a W W or Z Z boson and a Higgs boson in final states with leptons and b b -jets in 36 fb -1 of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration

title: Standing Shocks in Magnetized Dissipative Accretion Flow around Black Holes
creator: Biplob Sarkar *, Santabrata Das
description: Abstract We explore the global structure of the accretion flow around a Schwarzschild black hole where the accretion disc is threaded by toroidal magnetic fields. The accretion flow is optically thin and advection dominated. Synchrotron radiation is considered to be the active cooling mechanism in the flow.

title: Search for heavy Z ​ Z ZZ resonances in the ℓ + ​ ℓ − ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − \ell^{+}\ell^{-}\ell^{+}\ell^{-} and ℓ + ​ ℓ − ​ ν ​ ν ¯ \ell^{+}\ell^{-}\nu\bar{\nu} final states using proton–proton collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
description: Abstract A search for heavy resonances decaying into a pair of Z Z bosons leading to ℓ + ​ ℓ − ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − \ell^{+}\ell^{-}\ell^{+}\ell^{-} and ℓ + ​ ℓ − ​ ν ​ ν ¯ \ell^{+}\ell^{-}\nu\bar{\nu} final states, where ℓ \ell stands for either an electron or a muon, is presented.

title: Measurement of the inclusive and fiducial t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} production cross-sections in the lepton+jets channel in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 8 TeV \sqrt{s}=$8\text{\,}\mathrm{TeV}$ with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract The inclusive and fiducial t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} production cross-sections are measured in the lepton+jets channel using 20.2 fb − 1 20.2\text{\,}{\mathrm{fb}}^{-1} of proton–proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 8 TeV 8\text{\,}\mathrm{TeV} recorded with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

title: Magnetic Compton profiles of disordered Fe 0.5 Ni 0.5 and ordered FeNi alloys
creator: D. Benea a , J. Minár b , H. Ebert c , L. Chioncel d,e
description: Abstract We study the magnetic Compton profile (MCP) of the disordered Fe 0.5 Ni 0.5 and of the ordered FeNi alloys and discuss the interplay between structural disorder and electronic correlations. The Coherent Potential Approximation is employed to model the substitutional disorder within the single-site approximation, while local electronic correlations are captured with the Dynamical Mean Field Theory.

title: Ordered states in the Kitaev-Heisenberg model: From 1D chains to 2D honeycomb
creator: Cliò Efthimia Agrapidis, Jeroen van den Brink, Satoshi Nishimoto
description: Abstract We study the ground state of the 1D Kitaev-Heisenberg (KH) model using the density-matrix renormalization group and Lanczos exact diagonalization methods. We obtain a rich ground-state phase diagram as a function of the ratio between Heisenberg ( OPEN J = cos ⁡ ϕ ) J=\cos\phi) and Kitaev ( K = sin ⁡ ϕ K=\sin\phi ) interactions.

title: Limits of the trivial bundle on a curve
creator: Arnaud Beauville
description: Abstract We attempt to describe the vector bundles on a curve C C which are specializations of 𝒪 C 2 \mathcal{O}_{C}^{2}\, . We get a complete classification when C C is Brill-Noether-Petri general, or when it is hyperelliptic; in both cases all limit vector bundles are decomposable. We give examples of indecomposable limit bundles for some special curves. Keywords.

title: Wave function representation of probability distributions
creator: Madeleine B. Thompson
description: Abstract Orthogonal decomposition of the square root of a probability density function in the Hermite basis is a useful low-dimensional parameterization of continuous probability distributions over the reals. This representation is formally similar to the representation of quantum mechanical states as wave functions, whose squared modulus is a probability density.

title: Categorical Fermionic actions and minimal modular extensions
creator: César Galindo, César F. Venegas-Ramírez
description: Abstract . The purpose of this paper is to study minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories, with emphasis on minimal modular extensions of super-Tannakian fusion categories. We define actions of finite super-groups on fermionic fusion categories and spin-braided fusion categories.

title: Imperfect Thermalizations Allow for Optimal Thermodynamic Processes
creator: Elisa Bäumer, Martí Perarnau-Llobet, Philipp Kammerlander, Henrik Wilming, Renato Renner
description: Abstract Optimal (reversible) processes in thermodynamics can be modelled as step-by-step processes, where the system is successively thermalized with respect to different Hamiltonians by an external thermal bath. However, in practice interactions between system and thermal bath will take finite time, and precise control of their interaction is usually out of reach.

title: HEP Software Foundation Community White Paper Working Group – Software Development, Deployment and Validation
creator: HEP Software Foundation, Benjamin Couturier, Giulio Eulisse, Hadrien Grasland, Benedikt Hegner, Michel Jouvin, Meghan Kane, Daniel S. Katz, Thomas Kuhr, David Lange, Patricia Mendez Lorenzo, Martin Ritter, Graeme Andrew Stewart, and Andrea Valassi
description: Abstract The High Energy Physics community has developed and needs to maintain many tens of millions of lines of code and to integrate effectively the work of thousands of developers across large collaborations. Software needs to be built, validated, and deployed across hundreds of sites.

title: Assessing public health interventions using Web content Conference: ; ;
creator: Vasileios Lampos
description: Abstract . Public health interventions are a fundamental tool for mitigating the spread of an infectious disease. However, it is not always possible to obtain a conclusive estimate for the impact of an intervention, especially in situations where the effects are fragmented in population parts that are under-represented within traditional public health surveillance schemes.

title: Classification and characterization of nonequilibrium Higgs modes in unconventional superconductors
creator: L. Schwarz, B. Fauseweh, N. Tsuji, N. Cheng, N. Bittner, H. Krull, M. Berciu, G. S. Uhrig, A. P. Schnyder, S. Kaiser, D. Manske
description: Abstract Recent findings of new Higgs modes in unconventional superconductors require a classification and characterization of the modes allowed by nontrivial gap symmetry. Here we develop a theory for a tailored nonequilibrium quantum quench to excite all possible oscillation symmetries of a superconducting condensate.

title: Dynamical Mean-Field Theory on the Real-Frequency Axis: p-d Hybridizations and Atomic Physics in SrMnO 3
creator: Daniel Bauernfeind, Robert Triebl, Manuel Zingl, Markus Aichhorn, Hans Gerd Evertz
description: Abstract We investigate the electronic structure of SrMnO 3 \text{SrMnO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} with Density Functional Theory (DFT) plus Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT). Within this scheme the selection of the correlated subspace and the construction of the corresponding Wannier functions is a crucial step.

title: Can one design a geometry engine?
creator: Johann A. Makowsky
description: Abstract We survey the status of decidabilty of the consequence relation in various axiomatizations of Euclidean geometry. We draw attention to a widely overlooked result by Martin Ziegler from 1980, which proves Tarski’s conjecture on the undecidability of finitely axiomatizable theories of fields.

title: Measurement of the production cross section of three isolated photons in p ​ p pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} = 8 TeV using the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A measurement of the production of three isolated photons in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy s \sqrt{s} = 8 TeV is reported. The results are based on an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb -1 collected with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

title: Next to leading order QED corrections to the process γ ​ γ → μ + ​ μ − ​ γ \gamma\gamma\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\gamma
creator: Mikhail G. Kozlov
description: Abstract We have calculated one loop quantum electrodynamic corrections to the process γ ​ γ → μ + ​ μ − ​ γ \gamma\gamma\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\gamma , where all photons are on mass shell and the muon mass is taken into account.

title: Electro-mechanical Casimir effect
creator: Mikel Sanz, Witlef Wieczorek, Simon Gröblacher, Enrique Solano
description: Abstract The dynamical Casimir effect is an intriguing phenomenon in which photons are generated from vacuum due to a non-adiabatic change in some boundary conditions. In particular, it connects the motion of an accelerated mechanical mirror to the generation of photons. While pioneering experiments demonstrating this effect exist, a conclusive measurement involving a mechanical generation is still missing.

title: Discrete Gradient Line Fields on Surfaces
creator: Thomas Lewiner, Tiago Novello, João Paixão, Carlos Tomei
description: Abstract A line field on a manifold is a smooth map which assigns a tangent line to all but a finite number of points of the manifold. As such, it can be seen as a generalization of vector fields. They model a number of geometric and physical properties, e.g.

title: Multi-task learning of time series and its application to the travel demand
creator: Boris Chidlovskii
description: Abstract We address the problem of modeling and prediction of a set of temporal events in the context of intelligent transportation systems. To leverage the information shared by different events, we propose a multi-task learning framework. We develop a support vector regression model for joint learning of mutually dependent time series.

title: Combining Static and Dynamic Features for Multivariate Sequence Classification
creator: Anna Leontjeva, Ilya Kuzovkin
description: Abstract Model precision in a classification task is highly dependent on the feature space that is used to train the model. Moreover, whether the features are sequential or static will dictate which classification method can be applied as most of the machine learning algorithms are designed to deal with either one or another type of data.

title: Hankel determinants for a perturbed Laguerre weight and Painlevé V equation
creator: Min Chen, Yang Chen, En-Gui Fan
description: Abstract In this paper, we study Hankel determinants generated from the following perturbed Laguerre weight function, w ⁡ ( x , t ) = ( x + t ) λ ​ x α ​ e − x , t > 0 , α > 0 , α + λ + 1 > 0 , x ∈ [ 0 , ∞

title: Water Bottle Flipping Physics
creator: P.J. Dekker 1 , L.A.G. Eek 1 , M.M. Flapper 1 , H.J.C. Horstink 1 , A.R. Meulenkamp 1 , J. van der Meulen 1 , E.S. Kooij 1,2 , J.H. Snoeijer 1,3 , A. Marin 1,3
description: Abstract The water bottle flipping challenge consists of spinning a bottle, partially filled with water, and making it land upright. It is quite a striking phenomenon, since at first sight it appears rather improbable that a tall rotating bottle could make such a stable landing.

title: Variational Attention for Sequence-to-Sequence Models
creator: Hareesh Bahuleyan, Lili Mou, Olga Vechtomova, Pascal Poupart
description: Abstract The variational encoder-decoder (VED) encodes source information as a set of random variables using a neural network, which in turn is decoded into target data using another neural network. In natural language processing, sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) models typically serve as encoder-decoder networks.

title: A simple script language for choreography of multiple, synchronizing non-anthropomorphic robots — Working draft —
creator: Henning Christiansen
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Henning Christiansen. The scripting language described in this document is (in the first place) intended to be used on robots developed by Anja M¿lle Lindelof and Henning Christiansen as part of a research project about robots performing on stage. The target robots are expected to appear as familiar domestic objects that take their own life, so to speak, and perhaps perform together with human players, creating at illusion of a communication between them.

title: Tracking the Diffusion of Named Entities Conference: ; December 2017;
creator: Matthew Rowe, Leon Derczynski
description: Abstract . Existing studies of how information diffuses across social networks have thus far concentrated on analysing and recovering the spread of deterministic innovations such as URLs, hashtags, and group membership. However investigating how mentions of real-world entities appear and spread has yet to be explored, largely due to the computationally intractable nature of performing large-scale entity extraction.

title: A bivariate polynomial interpolation problem for matrices
creator: Dharm Prakash Singh, Amit Ujlayan ∗
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Dharm Prakash Singh, Amit Ujlayan ∗. In this article, we propose a bivariate polynomial interpolation problem for matrices (BVPIPM), for real matrices of the order m × n m\times n . In the process of solving the proposed problem, we establish the existence of a class of m ​ n mn -dimensional bivariate polynomial subspaces (BVPS) in which the BVPIPM always posses a unique solution.

title: Long-time asymptotic behavior for the complex short pulse equation
creator: Jian Xu, Engui Fan*
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Jian Xu, Engui Fan*. In this paper, we consider the initial value problem for the complex short pulse equation with a Wadati-Konno-Ichikawa type Lax pair. We show that the solution to the initial value problem has a parametric expression in terms of the solution of 2 × 2 2\times 2 -matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem, from which an implicit one-soliton solution is obtained on the discrete spectrum.

title: The construction and deformation of BiHom-Novikov agebras
creator: Shuangjian Guo, Xiaohui Zhang, Shengxiang Wang 1. School of Mathematics and Statistics, Guizhou University of Finance and EconomicsGuiyang 550025, P. R. of China2. School of Mathematical Sciences, Qufu Normal UniversityQufu 273165, P. R. of China3. School of Mathematics and Finance, Chuzhou Universi
description: Abstract ABSTRACT BiHom-Novikov agebra is a generalized Hom-Novikov algebra endowed with two commuting multiplicative linear maps. The main purpose of this paper is to show that two classes of BiHom-Novikov algebras can be constructed from BiHom-commutative algebras together with derivations and BiHom-Novikov algebras with Rota-Baxter operators, respectively.

title: Modeling interacting dark energy models with Chebyshev polynomials: Exploring their constraints and effects
creator: Freddy Cueva Solano
description: Abstract In this work, we examine the main cosmological effects derived from a time-varying coupling ( Q ¯ \bar{Q} ) between a dark matter (DM) fluid and a dark energy (DE) fluid with time-varying DE equation of state (EoS) parameter ( ω DE \mathrm{\omega_{DE}} ), in two different coupled DE models. These scenarios were built in terms of Chebyschev polynomials.

title: Exploring the Lyapunov instability properties of high-dimensional atmospheric and climate models
description: Abstract The stability properties of intermediate-order climate models are investigated by computing their Lyapunov exponents (LEs). The two models considered are PUMA (Portable University Model of the Atmosphere), a primitive-equation simple general circulation model, and MAOOAM (Modular Arbitrary-Order Ocean-Atmosphere Model), a quasi-geostrophic coupled ocean-atmosphere model on a β \beta -plane.

title: Geometrical Insights for Implicit Generative Modeling
creator: Leon Bottou a,b, Martin Arjovsky b, David Lopez-Paz a, Maxime Oquab a,c
description: Abstract Learning algorithms for implicit generative models can optimize a variety of criteria that measure how the data distribution differs from the implicit model distribution, including the Wasserstein distance, the Energy distance, and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy criterion. A careful look at the geometries induced by these distances on the space of probability measures reveals interesting differences.

title: z ∘ z^{\circ} -ideals in intermediate rings of ordered field valued continuous functions Thanks: The first author thanks the NBHM, Mumbai-400 001, India, for financial support
creator: Sagarmoy Bag, Sudip Kumar Acharyya, Dhananjoy Mandal
description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 54C40; Secondary 46E25 1. Abstract A proper ideal I in a commutative ring with unity is called a z^{\circ} -ideal if for each a in I , the intersection of all minimal prime ideals in R which contain a is contained in I .

title: The geometry of random minimal factorizations of a long cycle via biconditioned bitype random trees
creator: \firstname Valentin \lastname Féray, \firstname Igor \lastname Kortchemski
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by \firstname Valentin \lastname Féray, \firstname Igor \lastname Kortchemski. We study random typical minimal factorizations of the n n -cycle into transpositions, which are factorizations of ( 1 , … , n ) (1,\ldots,n) as a product of n − 1 n-1 transpositions. By viewing transpositions as chords of the unit disk and by reading them one after the other, one obtains a sequence of increasing laminations of the unit disk (i.e. compact subsets of the unit disk made of non-intersecting chords).

title: Some Consequences of Categorification This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Cluster Algebras. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/cluster-algebras.html
creator: Dylan RUPEL † and Salvatore STELLA ‡
description: Abstract Several conjectures on acyclic skew-symmetrizable cluster algebras are proven as direct consequences of their categorification via valued quivers. These include conjectures of Fomin–Zelevinsky, Reading–Speyer, and Reading–Stella related to 𝐝 \mathbf{d} -vectors, 𝐠 \mathbf{g} -vectors, and F F -polynomials. keywords acyclc cluster algebras; categorification; valued quivers AMS 13F60; 16G20 † † shorttitle: Some Consequences of Categorification † † runningauthor: D.

title: Search for physics beyond the standard model in events with high-momentum Higgs bosons and missing transverse momentum in proton-proton collisions at 13 \TeV
description: Abstract A search for physics beyond the standard model in events with one or more high-momentum Higgs bosons, \PH , decaying to pairs of \PQb quarks in association with missing transverse momentum is presented. The data, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.

title: Counting Periodic Trajectories of Finsler Billiards This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Algebra, Topology, and Dynamics in Interaction in honor of Dmitry Fuchs. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Fuchs.html
creator: Pavle V.M. BLAGOJEVIĆ † 1 † 2 {}^{{\dagger}^{1}{\dagger}^{2}}, Michael HARRISON † 3 {}^{{\dagger}^{3}}, Serge TABACHNIKOV † 4 {}^{{\dagger}^{4}} and Günter M. ZIEGLER † 1 {}^{{\dagger}^{1}}
description: Abstract We provide lower bounds on the number of periodic Finsler billiard trajectories inside a quadratically convex smooth closed hypersurface M M in a d d -dimensional Finsler space with possibly irreversible Finsler metric. An example of such a system is a billiard in a sufficiently weak magnetic field.

title: A Compositional Coalgebraic Semantics for Strategic Games We thank David Colander, Samson Abramsky, Alexander Kurz, Dusko Pavlovic, Paulo Oliva and Jules Hedges for discussions as well as the participants at the Games for Logic and Programming Languages VIII Workshop 2013 in London, the 19th Interna
creator: Achim Blumensath, Viktor Winschel
description: Abstract . We provide a compositional coalgebraic semantics for strategic games. In our framework, like in the semantics of functional programming languages, coalgebras represent the observable behaviour of systems derived from the behaviour of the parts over an unobservable state space.

title: A syntactic approach to the MacNeille completion of Λ ∗ \Lambda^{\ast} , the free monoid over an ordered alphabet Λ \Lambda .
creator: Hans-Jürgen Bandelt, Maurice Pouzet
description: Abstract . Let Λ ∗ \Lambda^{\ast} be the free monoid of (finite) words over a not necessarily finite alphabet Λ \Lambda , which is equipped with some (partial) order. This ordering lifts to Λ ∗ \Lambda^{\ast} , where it extends the divisibility ordering of words.

title: On the Universality of Memcomputing Machines
creator: Yan Ru Pei, Fabio L. Traversa, Massimiliano Di Ventra
description: Abstract Universal memcomputing machines (UMMs) [IEEE Trans. Neural Netw. Learn. Syst. 26 , 2702 (2015)] represent a novel computational model in which memory (time non-locality) accomplishes both tasks of storing and processing of information. UMMs have been shown to be Turing-complete, namely they can simulate any Turing machine.

title: Erratum to: Search for PeVatrons at the Galactic Center using a radio air-shower array at the South Pole Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
creator: A. Balagopal V. ∗, A. Haungs, T. Huege, F. G. Schröder
description: Abstract ∎ Erratum to: Eur. Phys. J. C (2018) 78: 111 It was shown in Balagopal V. et al. 2018 that an optimal signal-to-noise ratio is obtained in the frequency band of 100-190 MHz, which allows us to lower the energy threshold of radio observations of air showers.

title: A Data-driven Approach to Multi-event Analytics in Large-scale Power Systems Using Factor Model
creator: Fan Yang, Xing He, Robert Caiming Qiu, Zenan Ling
description: Abstract Multi-event detection and recognition in real time is of challenge for a modern grid as its feature is usually non-identifiable. Based on factor model, this paper porposes a data-driven method as an alternative solution under the framework of random matrix theory.

title: Porous translucent electrodes enhance current generation from photosynthetic biofilms
creator: Tobias Wenzel, Daniel Haertter, Paolo Bombelli, Christopher J. Howe *, Ullrich Steiner *
description: Abstract We tested the enhancement of electrical current generated from photosynthetically active bacteria by use of electrodes with porosity on the nano- and micrometer length-scale. For two cyanobacteria on structured indium-tin-oxide electrodes, current generation was increased by two orders of magnitude and the photo-response was substantially faster compared to non-porous anodes.

title: A Few Characterizations of Topological Spaces with No Infinite Discrete Subspace Thanks: The first author was supported by grant ANR-17-CE40-0028 of the French National Research Agency ANR (project BRAVAS)
creator: Jean Goubault-Larrecq, Maurice Pouzet
description: Abstract . We give several characteristic properties of FAC spaces, namely topological spaces with no infinite discrete subspace. The first one was obtained in 2019 by the first author, and states that every closed set is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets. The full result extends well-known characterizations of posets with no infinite antichain.

title: Search for R R -parity violating supersymmetry in pp collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV using \cPqb jets in a final state with a single lepton, many jets, and high sum of large-radius jet masses
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by . Results are reported from a search for physics beyond the standard model in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV . The search uses a signature of a single lepton, large jet and bottom quark jet multiplicities, and high sum of large-radius jet masses, without any requirement on the missing transverse momentum in an event. The data sample corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv recorded by the CMS experiment at the LHC.

title: Measurement of prompt and nonprompt charmonium suppression in PbPb collisions at 5.02 \TeV
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by . The nuclear modification factors of \JPsi and ψ ​ (2S) \psi\text{(2S)} mesons are measured in PbPb collisions at a centre-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of s NN = 5.02 ​ \TeV \sqrt{\smash[b]{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}}=5.02\TeV . The analysis is based on PbPb and \Pp ​ \Pp \Pp\Pp data samples collected by CMS at the LHC in 2015, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 464 \mubinv and 28 \pbinv , respectively.

title: Denoising of image gradients and total generalized variation denoising Thanks: This material was based upon work partially supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant DMS-1127914 to the Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute. Any opinions, findings, and conclusions or r
creator: B. Komander, D. A. Lorenz, L. Vestweber
description: Abstract We revisit total variation denoising and study an augmented model where we assume that an estimate of the image gradient is available. We show that this increases the image reconstruction quality and derive that the resulting model resembles the total generalized variation denoising method, thus providing a new motivation for this model.

title: Universality at large transverse spin in defect CFT Preprint: DESY 17-239 HU-EP-17/31
creator: Madalena Lemos, Pedro Liendo, Marco Meineri, Sourav Sarkar
description: Abstract We study the spectrum of local operators living on a defect in a generic conformal field theory, and their coupling to the local bulk operators. We establish the existence of universal accumulation points in the spectrum at large s s , s s being the charge of the operators under rotations in the space transverse to the defect.

title: Scaling law of the drag force in dense granular media
creator: Sonu Kumar, K. Anki Reddy, Satoshi Takada, Hisao Hayakawa
description: Abstract Making use of the system of pulling a spherical intruder in static three-dimensional granular media, we numerically study the scaling law for the drag force F drag F_{\rm drag} acting on the moving intruder under the influence of the gravity.

title: SIMULATION ON VARIOUS TOPOCENTRIC POINTS OF THE ZODIAC CONSTELLATIONS Simulación en Diversos Puntos Topocéntricos de las Constelaciones Zodiacales
creator: H. Laserna, S. Silva, Y. Cruz
description: Abstract Abstract. On the sighting of the constellations and their stars, they seem to be near each other at first sight but some of them are actually quite further from the others. From the geocentric point of view can the Zodiac Constellations be perceived as referential marks divided into the terrestrial ecliptic, which are organized according to their shapes.

title: Mapping to Declarative Knowledge for Word Problem Solving
creator: Subhro RoyMassachusetts Institute of Technology subhro@csail.mit.edu, Dan RothUniversity of Pennsylvania danroth@seas.upenn.edu
description: Abstract Math word problems form a natural abstraction to a range of quantitative reasoning problems, such as understanding financial news, sports results, and casualties of war. Solving such problems requires the understanding of several mathematical concepts such as dimensional analysis, subset relationships, etc.

title: Search for electroweak production of supersymmetric states in scenarios with compressed mass spectra at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for electroweak production of supersymmetric particles in scenarios with compressed mass spectra in final states with two low-momentum leptons and missing transverse momentum is presented. This search uses proton–proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider in 2015–2016 , corresponding to 36.

title: Dust-acoustic rogue waves in an opposite polarity dusty plasma featuring non-extensive statistics Journal: Annals of Physics
creator: D. M. S. Zaman ∗ , A. Mannan, and A. A. Mamun
description: Abstract Modulational instability (MI) of dust acoustic waves (DAWs), which propagates in an opposite polarity dusty plasma system, containing inertial warm negatively and positively charged dust particles as well as non-extensive q-distributed electrons and ions, has been theoretically investigated. The nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation is derived by employing the reductive perturbation method.

title: Cosmological Analysis of Modified Holographic Ricci Dark Energy in Chern-Simons Modified Gravity
creator: Sarfraz Ali and M. Jamil Amir
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the cosmological analysis of the modified holographic Ricci dark energy model and reconstruct different scalar field models in the context of Chern-Simon modified gravity. We investigate the deceleration parameter, which shows that the universe is in the accelerating expansion phase.

title: Companions, Codensity and Causality
creator: Damien Pous \rsuper a, Jurriaan Rot \rsuper b
description: Abstract . In the context of abstract coinduction in complete lattices, the notion of compatible function makes it possible to introduce enhancements of the coinduction proof principle. The largest compatible function, called the companion, subsumes most enhancements and has been proved to enjoy many good properties.

title: A Simple and Natural Interpretations of the DAMPE Cosmic Ray Electron/Positron Spectrum within Two Sigma Deviations
creator: Jia-Shu Niu, Tianjun Li, Fang-Zhou Xu
description: Abstract The DArk Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE) experiment has recently announced the first results for the measurement of total electron plus positron fluxes between 25 GeV and 4.6 TeV. A spectral break at about 0.9 TeV and a tentative peak excess around 1.4 TeV have been found.

title: Episodic accretion in binary protostars emerging from self-gravitating solar mass cores
creator: R. Riaz, S. Vanaverbeke, D.R.G. Schleicher
description: Abstract Observations show a large spread in the luminosities of young protostars, which are frequently explained in the context of episodic accretion. We here test this scenario using numerical simulations following the collapse of a solar mass molecular cloud using the GRADSPH code, varying the strength of the initial perturbations and the temperature of the cores.

title: The Chazy XII Equation and Schwarz Triangle Functions

description: Abstract A search for the Standard Model Higgs boson produced in association with a top-quark pair, t ​ t ¯ ​ H t\bar{t}H , is presented. The analysis uses 36.1 fb -1 of p ​ p pp collision data at s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV collected with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider in 2015 and 2016.

title: Forecasting the Contribution of Polarized Extragalactic Radio Sources in CMB observations
creator: G. Puglisi, V. Galluzzi, L. Bonavera, J. Gonzalez-Nuevo, A. Lapi, M. Massardi, F. Perrotta , C. Baccigalupi, A. Celotti, L. Danese
description: Abstract We combine the latest datasets obtained with different surveys to study the frequency dependence of polarized emission coming from Extragalactic Radio Sources (ERS). We consider data over a very wide frequency range starting from 1.4 1.4 GHz up to 217 217 GHz.

title: Coalgebraic Behavioral Metrics
creator: Paolo Baldan, Filippo Bonchi, Henning Kerstan, Barbara König
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Paolo Baldan, Filippo Bonchi, Henning Kerstan, Barbara König. We study different behavioral metrics, such as those arising from both branching and linear-time semantics, in a coalgebraic setting. Given a coalgebra α : X → H ​ X \alpha\colon X\to HX for a functor H : S ​ e ​ t → S ​ e ​ t H\colon\mathnormal{Set}\to\mathnormal{Set} , we define a framework for deriving pseudometrics on X X which measure the behavioral distance of states.

title: Adaptive PBDW approach to state estimation: noisy observations; user-defined update spaces
description: Abstract We provide a number of extensions and further interpretations of the Parameterized-Background Data-Weak (PBDW) formulation, a real-time and in-situ Data Assimilation (DA) framework for physical systems modeled by parametrized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), proposed in [Y Maday, AT Patera, JD Penn, M Yano, Int J Numer Meth Eng, 102(5), 933-965].

title: On 𝒒 \boldsymbol{q} -Deformations of the Heun Equation This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Elliptic Hypergeometric Functions and Their Applications. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/EHF2017.html
creator: Kouichi TAKEMURA
description: Abstract The q q -Heun equation and its variants arise as degenerations of Ruijsenaars–van Diejen operators with one particle. We investigate local properties of these equations. In particular we characterize the variants of the q q -Heun equation by using analysis of regular singularities. We also consider the quasi-exact solvability of the q q -Heun equation and its variants.

title: Optimized Entanglement Purification
creator: Stefan Krastanov, Victor V. Albert, Liang Jiang
description: Abstract We investigate novel protocols for entanglement purification of qubit Bell pairs. Employing genetic algorithms for the design of the purification circuit, we obtain shorter circuits achieving higher success rates and better final fidelities than what is currently available in the literature.

title: Analysis of Concurrent Lock-Free Hash Tries with Constant-Time Operations
creator: Aleksandar Prokopec
description: Abstract . Ctrie is a scalable concurrent non-blocking dictionary data structure, with good cache locality, and non-blocking linearizable iterators ( Prokopec et al. 2012 ) . However, operations on most existing concurrent hash tries run in O ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) O(\log n) time. In this technical report, we extend the standard concurrent hash-tries ( Prokopec et al.

title: Enumerating consistent subgraphs of directed acyclic graphs: an insight into biomedical ontologies
creator: Yisu Peng, Yuxiang Jiang, Predrag Radivojac
description: Abstract Modern problems of concept annotation associate an object of interest (gene, individual, text document) with a set of interrelated textual descriptors (functions, diseases, topics), often organized in concept hierarchies or ontologies. Most ontologies can be seen as directed acyclic graphs, where nodes represent concepts and edges represent relational ties between these concepts.

title: PyPhi: A toolbox for integrated information theory
creator: William G. P. Mayner
description: Abstract Abstract Integrated information theory provides a mathematical framework to fully characterize the cause-effect structure of a physical system. Here, we introduce PyPhi , a Python software package that implements this framework for causal analysis and unfolds the full cause-effect structure of discrete dynamical systems of binary elements.

title: Efficient Parallel Connected Components Labeling with a Coarse-to-fine Strategy Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates

This paper proposes a new parallel approach to solve connected components on a 2D binary image implemented with CUDA. We employ the following strategies to accelerate neighborhood exploration after dividing an input image into independent blocks.

We prove that two different MELL proof-nets have two different Taylor expansions. As a corollary, we prove a completeness result for MELL: We show that the relational model is injective for MELL proof-nets, i.e.

title: On the statistical properties of turbulent energy transfer rate in the inner Heliosphere
creator: Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Francesco Carbone, Silvia Perri, Antonella Greco, Raffaele Marino, Roberto Bruno
description: Abstract The transfer of energy from large to small scales in solar wind turbulence is an important ingredient of the longstanding question about the mechanism of the interplanetary plasma heating. Previous studies have shown that magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is statistically compatible with the observed solar wind heating as it expands in the heliosphere.

title: Evidence for the associated production of the Higgs boson and a top quark pair with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for the associated production of the Higgs boson with a top quark pair ( t ​ t ¯ ​ H t\bar{t}H ) is reported. The search is performed in multilepton final states using a dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 36.

title: Explicit Induction is Not Equivalent to Cyclic Proofs for Classical Logic with Inductive Definitions
creator: Stefano Berardi \rsuper a, Makoto Tatsuta \rsuper b
description: Abstract . A cyclic proof system, called CLKID-omega, gives us another way of representing inductive definitions and efficient proof search. The 2005 paper by Brotherston showed that the provability of CLKID-omega includes the provability of LKID, first order classical logic with inductive definitions in Martin-Löf’s style, and conjectured the equivalence. The equivalence has been left an open question since 2011.

title: RedDwarfData: a simplified dataset of StarCraft matches
creator: Juan J. Merelo-Guervós, Antonio Fernández-Ares
description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Juan J. Merelo-Guervós, Antonio Fernández-Ares. The game Starcraft is one of the most interesting arenas to test new machine learning and computational intelligence techniques; however, StarCraft matches take a long time and creating a good dataset for training can be hard.

creator: Martin Dittus, Joss Wright, Mark Graham
description: Abstract . Does recent growth of darknet markets signify a slow reorganisation of the illicit drug trade? Where are darknet markets situated in the global drug supply chain? In principle, these platforms allow producers to sell directly to end users, bypassing traditional trafficking routes.

title: Electroweak production of two jets in association with a Z boson in proton-proton collisions at s = \sqrt{s}= 13 \TeV
description: Abstract A measurement of the electroweak (EW) production of two jets in association with a \PZ \PZ boson in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV is presented, based on data recorded in 2016 by the CMS experiment at the LHC corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv .
