description: Abstract We show that, for any subsets S S and T T of 𝔽 q n \mathbb{F}_{q}^{n} , there are subsets S ′ ⊂ S S^{\prime}\subset S and T ′ ⊂ T T^{\prime}\subset T such that | S ′ | + | T ′ | < c q n |S^{\prime}|+|T^{\prime}|<c_{q}^{n} for some c q < q c_{q}<q , and (

title: Measurement Of Energy Resolution For TES Microcalorimeter With Optical Pulses Thanks: CAS Strategic Priority A(Grant No. XDA040762)
creator: Shuo Zhang 3;1) Qing-Ya Zhang 1,2;1) Jianshe Liu 1,2 CongZhan Liu 3 Wenhui Dong 1,2 Wei Chen 1,2
description: Abstract Energy resolution is an important figure of merit for TES microcalorimeter. We propose a laser system to measure the energy resolution of TES microcalorimeter with a 1550 nm laser source. Compared to method that characterizes the performance by irradiating the detector using X-ray photons from a radioactive source placed inside the refrigerator, our system is safer and more convenient.

title: Photon pair generation in hydrogenated amorphous silicon microring resonators
creator: Elizabeth Hemsley, Damien Bonneau, Jason Pelc, Ray Beausoleil, Jeremy L. O’Brien, Mark G. Thompson
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Elizabeth Hemsley, Damien Bonneau, Jason Pelc, Ray Beausoleil, Jeremy L. O’Brien, Mark G. Thompson. We generate photon pairs in a-Si:H microrings using a CW pump, and find the Kerr coefficient of a-Si:H to be 3.73 ± 0.25 × 10 − 17 ​ m 2 / W 3.73\pm 0.25\times 10^{-17}m^{2}/W . By measuring the Q factor with coupled power we find that the loss in the a-Si:H micro-rings scales linearly with power, and therefore cannot originate from two photon absorption.

title: On Free ω \omega -Continuous and Regular Ordered Algebras
creator: Zoltán Ésik \rsuper a, Dexter Kozen \rsuper b
description: Abstract . We study varieties of certain ordered Σ \Sigma -algebras with restricted completeness and continuity properties. We give a general characterization of their free algebras in terms of submonads of the monad of Σ \Sigma -coterms. Varieties of this form are called quasi-regular .

title: Magnetic Catalysis in the Higher-Order Quark Sigma Model
creator: M. Abu-Shady
description: Abstract The effect of the higher-order mesonic interactions is investigated on the chiral symmetry breaking in the presence of an external magnetic field. The effective of higher-order mesonic potential is employed and is numerically solved in the mean-field approximation. The chiral symmetry breaking increases with increasing magnetic field. Two sets of free parameterization are investigated on the magnetic catalysis.

title: Consensus Based Medical Image Segmentation Using Semi-Supervised Learning And Graph Cuts
creator: Dwarikanath Mahapatra
description: Abstract Medical image segmentation requires consensus ground truth segmentations to be derived from multiple expert annotations. A novel approach is proposed that obtains consensus segmentations from experts using graph cuts (GC) and semi supervised learning (SSL). Popular approaches use iterative Expectation Maximization (EM) to estimate the final annotation and quantify annotator’s performance.

title: Chromatic Numbers of Exact Distance Graphs Thanks: The research for this paper was started during a stay of the first two authors at the Mittag-Leffler Institute in Stockholm. JvdH and HAK would like to thank the Mittag-Leffler Institute for hospitality and support. DAQ thankfully acknowledges suppo
creator: Jan van den Heuvel, H.A. Kierstead, Daniel A. Quiroz
description: Abstract For any graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) and positive integer p p , the exact distance- p p graph G [ ♮ ​ p ] G^{[\natural p]} is the graph with vertex set V V , which has an edge between vertices x x and y y if and only if x x and y

title: Preferential attachment combined with the random number of choices Thanks: The presented work was performed under the State Assignment N3.8032.2017/BCh of the Ministry of Science and Education of Russia.
creator: Yury Malyshkin
description: Abstract . We study the asymptotic behavior of the maximal degree in the degree distribution in an evolving tree model combining local choice and Mori’s preferential attachment. In the considered model, the random graph is constructed in the following way. At each step, a new vertex is introduced.

title: How structure sculpts function: unveiling the contribution of anatomical connectivity to the brain’s spontaneous correlation structure
creator: R. G. Bettinardi, G. Deco, V. M. Karlaftis, T. J. Van Hartevelt, H. M. Fernandes, Z. Kourtzi, M. L. Kringelbach, G. Zamora-López
description: Abstract Intrinsic brain activity is characterized by highly structured co-activations between different regions, whose origin is still under debate. In this paper, we address the question whether it is possible to unveil how the underlying anatomical connectivity shape the brain’s spontaneous correlation structure.

title: I I -primary submodules
creator: Ismael Akray, Halgurd S. Hussein
description: Abstract In this paper, we give a generalization for weakly primary submodules called I I -primary submodule and we study some properties of it. We give some characterizations of I I -primary submodules. Also we establish the situation of I I -primary submodules in module localizations and decomposable modules. \citesort \authorheadline I. Akray and H. S.

title: An initial investigation of the performance of GPU-based swept time-space decomposition
creator: Daniel Magee and Kyle E. Niemeyer Oregon State University, Corvallis OR 97331-6001, USA
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Daniel Magee and Kyle E. Niemeyer Oregon State University, Corvallis OR 97331-6001, USA. Simulations of physical phenomena are essential to the expedient design of precision components in aerospace and other high-tech industries. These phenomena are often described by mathematical models involving partial differential equations (PDEs) without exact solutions. Modern design problems require simulations with a level of resolution that is difficult to achieve in a reasonable amount of time even in effectively parallelized solvers.

title: Interactive Elicitation of Knowledge on Feature Relevance Improves Predictions in Small Data Sets
creator: Luana Micallef* ,1 , Iiris Sundin* ,1 , Pekka Marttinen* ,1 , Muhammad Ammad-ud-din 1 , Tomi Peltola 1 , Marta Soare 1 , Giulio Jacucci 2 , and Samuel Kaski 1
description: Abstract Providing accurate predictions is challenging for machine learning algorithms when the number of features is larger than the number of samples in the data. Prior knowledge can improve machine learning models by indicating relevant variables and parameter values. Yet, this prior knowledge is often tacit and only available from domain experts.

title: Distributed Publish/Subscribe Query Processing on the Spatio-Textual Data Stream
creator: Zhida Chen, Gao Cong, Zhenjie Zhang, Tom Z.J. Fu, Lisi Chen, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Advanced Digital Sciences Center, Illinois at Singapore Pte. Ltd, Singapore, Guangdong University of Technology, China, Hong Kong Baptist University, Hong Kong, chen0936@e.ntu.edu.sg, gaocong@nt
description: Abstract Huge amount of data with both space and text information, e.g., geo-tagged tweets, is flooding on the Internet. Such spatio-textual data stream contains valuable information for millions of users with various interests on different keywords and locations. Publish/subscribe systems enable efficient and effective information distribution by allowing users to register continuous queries with both spatial and textual constraints.

title: Order statistics of horse racing and the randomly broken stick
creator: Peter A. Bebbington, Julius Bonart
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Peter A. Bebbington, Julius Bonart. We find a remarkable agreement between the statistics of a randomly divided interval and the observed statistical patterns and distributions found in horse racing betting markets. We compare the distribution of implied winning odds, the average true winning probabilities, the implied odds conditional on a win, and the average implied odds of the winning horse with the corresponding quantities from the “randomly broken stick problem”. We observe that the market is at least to some degree informationally efficient.

title: Semi-Supervised linear regression
creator: David Azriel, Lawrence D. Brown, Michael Sklar, Richard Berk, Andreas Buja, Linda Zhao
description: Abstract We study a regression problem where for some part of the data we observe both the label variable ( Y Y ) and the predictors ( 𝐗 {\bf X} ), while for other part of the data only the predictors are given.

title: Statistical properties of the Bipolar Magnetic Regions
creator: Dong Li
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Dong Li. Using the observations from Michelson Doppler Imager (MDI) onboard Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO), we develop a computational algorithm to automatically identify the bipolar magnetic regions (BMRs) in the active regions, and then study their statistical properties.

title: Measurement of the W W boson polarisation in t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} events from p ​ p pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} = 8 TeV in the lepton + jets channel with ATLAS
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by The ATLAS Collaboration. This paper presents a measurement of the polarisation of W W bosons from t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} decays, reconstructed in events with one high- p T p_{\mbox{T}} lepton and at least four jets. Data from p ​ p pp collisions at the LHC were collected at s \sqrt{s} = 8 TeV and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb -1 .

title: Domain knowledge assisted cyst segmentation in OCT retinal images
creator: Karthik Gopinath, Jayanthi Sivaswamy
description: Abstract 3D imaging modalities are becoming increasingly popular and relevant in retinal imaging owing to their effectiveness in highlighting structures in sub-retinal layers. OCT is one such modality which has great importance in the context of analysis of cystoid structures in subretinal layers.

title: Quasi-periodic pulsations with periods that change depending on whether the pulsations have thermal or nonthermal components
creator: D. Li, Q. M. Zhang, Y. Huang, Z. J. Ning, and Y. N. Su
description: Abstract Context. Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) typically display periodic and regular peaks in the light curves during the flare emissions. Sometimes, QPPs show multiple periods at the same wavelength. However, changing periods in various channels are rare. Aims. We report QPPs in a solar flare on 2014 October 27.

title: TCP-aware Cross Layer Scheduling with Adaptive Modulation in IEEE 802.16 (WiMAX) Networks
creator: Hemant Kumar Rath, Abhay Karandikar, Vishal Sharma
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Hemant Kumar Rath, Abhay Karandikar, Vishal Sharma. In this paper, we propose Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)-aware cross layer scheduling algorithms in a multipoint-to-point network such as the uplink of an IEEE 802.16 (WiMAX) network. Inadequate bandwidth allocation to a TCP flow may lead to timeout and since TCP source drops its congestion window ( c ​ w ​ n ​ d cwnd ) immediately after a timeout, it may affect the average throughput adversely.

title: A Sommerfeld Toolbox for Colored Dark Sectors Preprint: MITP/16-135 arXiv: 1612.02825
creator: Sonia El Hedri, Anna Kaminska, Maikel de Vries
description: Abstract We present analytical formulae for the Sommerfeld corrections to the annihilation of massive colored particles into quarks and gluons through the strong interaction. These corrections are essential to accurately compute the dark matter relic density for coannihilation with colored partners.

title: Katya Komendantskaya and František Farka,
creator: Edinburgh, 28 November 2016
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Edinburgh, 28 November 2016. CoALP-Ty’16 Pre-proceedings of the Workshop on Coalgebra, Horn Clause Logic Programming and Types November 28–29, 2016 Edinburgh, UK Ekaterina Komendantskaya and František Farka (ed.) https://ff32.host.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/coalpty16/ Organisation Organising Committee Workshop Chairs Ekaterina Komendantskaya, Heriot-Watt University, UK John Power, University of Bath, UK Publicity Chair František Farka, University of Dundee, UK and University of St Andrews, UK Programme Committee Ki Yung Ahn, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Davide Ancona, University of Genoa, Italy Filippo Bonchi, CNRS, ENS de Lyon, France Iavor Diatchki, Galois,

title: A note on holographic dark energy with varying c 2 c^{2} term
creator: A. Sheykhi 1,2 , S. Ghaffari 2 and N. Roshanshah 1
description: Abstract We reconsider the holographic dark energy (HDE) model with a slowly time varying c 2 ​ ( z ) c^{2}(z) parameter in the energy density, namely ρ D = 3 ​ M p 2 ​ c 2 ​ ( z ) / L 2 \rho_{D}=3M_{p}^{2}c^{2}(z)/L^{2} , where L L is the IR cutoff and z z is the redshift

title: STUDIA MATHEMATICA
creator: BULGARICA
description: Abstract The paper considers multivariate discrete random sums with equal number of summands. Such distributions describe the total claim amount received by a company in a fixed time point. In Queuing theory they characterize cumulative waiting times of customers up to time t. In Theory of branching processes they model the number of heirs at a fixed point in time.

title: Photon Blockade in Two-Emitter-Cavity Systems
creator: Marina Radulaski, Kevin A. Fischer, Konstantinos G. Lagoudakis, Jingyuan Linda Zhang, Jelena Vučković
description: Abstract The photon blockade (PB) effect in emitter-cavity systems depends on the anharmonicity of the ladder of dressed energy eigenstates. The recent developments in color center photonics are leading toward experimental demonstrations of multi-emitter-cavity solid-state systems with an expanded set of energy levels compared to the traditionally studied single-emitter systems.

title: Improved prediction accuracy for disease risk mapping using Gaussian Process stacked generalisation
creator: Samir Bhatt, Ewan Cameron, Seth R Flaxman, Daniel J Weiss, David L Smith, Peter W Gething
description: Abstract Maps of infectious disease—charting spatial variations in the force of infection, degree of endemicity, and the burden on human health—provide an essential evidence base to support planning towards global health targets. Contemporary disease mapping efforts have embraced statistical modelling approaches to properly acknowledge uncertainties in both the available measurements and their spatial interpolation.

title: On warped product manifolds satisfying some pseudosymmetric type conditions
creator: Absos Ali Shaikh and Haradhan Kundu
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Absos Ali Shaikh and Haradhan Kundu. The object of the present paper is to study the characterization of warped product manifolds satisfying some pseudosymmetric type conditions, especially, due to projective curvature tensor. For this purpose we consider a warped product manifold satisfying the pseudosymmetric type condition R ⋅ R = L 1 ​ Q ​ ( g , R ) + L 2 ​ Q ​ ( S , R ) R\cdot R=L_{1}Q(g,R)+L_{2}Q(S,R) and evaluate its characterization theorem.

title: Yosida duality
creator: Bas Westerbaan
description: Abstract In this note we prove Yosida duality — that is: the category of compact Hausdorff spaces with continuous maps is dually equivalent to the category of uniformly complete Archimedean Riesz spaces with distinguished units and unit-preserving Riesz homomorphisms between them. For a compact Hausdorff space X , write C(X) for the vector space of real-valued continuous functions on it.

title: On the Capacity and Depth of Compact Surfaces
creator: M. Abbasi, B. Mashayekhy
description: Abstract K. Borsuk in 1979, at the Topological Conference in Moscow, introduced the concept of capacity and depth of a compactum. In this paper we compute the capacity and depth of compact surfaces. We show that the capacity and depth of every compact orientable surface of genus g ≥ 0 g\geq 0 is equal to g + 2 g+2 .

title: Technical Report: A Generalized Matching Pursuit Approach for Graph-Structured Sparsity
creator: Feng Chen, Baojian Zhou
description: Abstract Sparsity-constrained optimization is an important and challenging problem that has wide applicability in data mining, machine learning, and statistics. In this paper, we focus on sparsity-constrained optimization in cases where the cost function is a general nonlinear function and, in particular, the sparsity constraint is defined by a graph-structured sparsity model.

title: Nilpotent orbit theorem in p p -adic Hodge theory
creator: Mohammad Reza Rahmati, Gerardo Flores
description: Abstract . We state and prove three orbit theorems on the period domains for the p p -adic Hodge structure analogous to the complex case. We shall consider the variation of de Rham (resp. étale) cohomology in a family of projective varieties f : 𝔛 → S f:\mathfrak{X}\to S defined over a p-adic field.

title: A uniform General Neron Desingularization in dimension one
creator: Asma Khalid, Gerhard Pfister, and Dorin Popescu
description: Abstract . We give a uniform General Neron Desingularization for one dimensional local rings with respect to morphisms which coincide modulo a high power of the maximal ideal. The result has interesting applications in the case of Cohen-Macaulay rings. Key words : Smooth morphisms, regular morphisms 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 13B40, Secondary 14B25,13H05,13J15.

title: A Model of Multi-Agent Consensus for Vague and Uncertain Beliefs
creator: Michael Crosscombe, Jonathan Lawry Department of Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol, BS8 1UB, United Kingdom m.crosscombe@bristol.ac.uk ⋅ \cdot j.lawry@bristol.ac.uk
description: Abstract Consensus formation is investigated for multi-agent systems in which agents’ beliefs are both vague and uncertain. Vagueness is represented by a third truth state meaning borderline . This is combined with a probabilistic model of uncertainty. A belief combination operator is then proposed which exploits borderline truth values to enable agents with conflicting beliefs to reach a compromise.

title: The Effect of Strange Quark on the Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Magnetic Background in the framework of logarithmic quark-sigma model
creator: M. Abu-Shady
description: Abstract The chiral symmetry breaking in the presence of an external magnetic field is studied in the framework of logarithmic quark-sigma model with three flavors ( u , d , s ) \left(u,d,s\right) . The effective logarithmic mesonic potential is extended to strange quark and is numerically solved in the mean-field approximation.

title: Unraveling reported dreams with text analytics
creator: Iris Hendrickx, Louis Onrust, Florian Kunneman, Ali Hürriyetoğlu, Antal van den Bosch, Wessel Stoop
description: Abstract We investigate what distinguishes reported dreams from other personal narratives. The continuity hypothesis , stemming from psychological dream analysis work, states that most dreams refer to a person’s daily life and personal concerns, similar to other personal narratives such as diary entries.

title: Non-Commutative Vector Bundles for Non-Unital Algebras
creator: Adam RENNIE and Aidan SIMS
description: Abstract We revisit the characterisation of modules over non-unital C ∗ C^{*} -algebras analogous to modules of sections of vector bundles. A fullness condition on the associated multiplier module characterises a class of modules which closely mirror the commutative case.

title: Connection Discovery using Shared Images by Gaussian Relational Topic Model
creator: Xiaopeng Li 1 , Ming Cheung 2 , James She 3
description: Abstract Social graphs, representing online friendships among users, are one of the fundamental types of data for many applications, such as recommendation, virality prediction and marketing in social media. However, this data may be unavailable due to the privacy concerns of users, or kept private by social network operators, which makes such applications difficult.

title: One-loop pentagon integral with one offshell leg in d d dimensions from differential equations in ϵ \epsilon -form
creator: Mikhail G. Kozlov
description: Abstract We apply differential equations technique to the calculation of the one-loop massless diagram with one offshell legs. Using reduction to ϵ \epsilon -form, we managed to obtain a simple one-fold integral representation exact in space-time dimensionality. Expansion of the obtained result in ϵ \epsilon and analytical continuation to physical region are discussed.

title: Isomonodromy for the Degenerate Fifth Painlevé Equation
creator: Primitivo B. ACOSTA-HUMÁNEZ †, Marius VAN DER PUT ‡ and Jaap TOP ‡
description: Abstract This is a sequel to papers by the last two authors making the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence and isomonodromy explicit. For the degenerate fifth Painlevé equation, the moduli spaces for connections and for monodromy are explicitly computed. It is proven that the extended Riemann–Hilbert morphism is an isomorphism.

title: Development and Operation of a P ​ r 2 ​ F ​ e 14 ​ B Pr_{2}Fe_{14}B Based Cryogenic Permanent Magnet Undulator for a High Spatial Resolution X-ray Beamline
creator: C. Benabderrahmane, M. Valléau, A. Ghaith, P. Berteaud, L. Chapuis, F. Marteau, F. Briquez, O. Marcouillé, J.-L. Marlats, K. Tavakoli, A. Mary, D. Zerbib, A. Lestrade, M. Louvet, P. Brunelle, K. Medjoubi, R. Nagaoka, C. Herbeaux, N. Béchu, P. Rommeluere, A. Somogyi, O. Chubar, C. Kitegi, M.-E. Coupr
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by C. Benabderrahmane, M. Valléau, A. Ghaith, P. Berteaud, L. Chapuis, F. Marteau, F. Briquez, O. Marcouillé, J.-L. Marlats, K. Tavakoli, A. Mary, D. Zerbib, A. Lestrade, M. Louvet, P. Brunelle, K. Medjoubi, R. Nagaoka, C. Herbeaux, N. Béchu, P. Rommeluere, A. Somogyi, O. Chubar, C. Kitegi, M.-E. Coupr. Short period, high field undulators are used to produce hard X-rays on synchrotron radiation based storage ring facilities of intermediate energy and enable short wavelength Free Electron Laser.

title: A Video-Based Method for Automatically Rating Ataxia
creator:
ame Ronnachai Jaroensri \email tiam@mit.edu, 
ame Amy Zhao \email xamyzhao@mit.edu, 
ame Guha Balakrishnan \email balakg@mit.edu, 
ame Derek Lo \email derektlo@gmail.com, 
ame Jeremy D. Schmahmann, M.D. \email jschmahmann@mgh.harvard.edu, 
ame Frédo Durand \email fredo@mit.edu, 
ame John Gut
description: Abstract For many movement disorders, such as Parkinson’s disease and ataxia, disease progression is visually assessed by a clinician using a numerical disease rating scale. These tests are subjective, time-consuming, and must be administered by a professional. This can be problematic where specialists are not available, or when a patient is not consistently evaluated by the same clinician.

title: Multi-bump solutions for fractional Nirenberg problem Thanks: 1 The first author is partially supported by the NSF of China (11471170).
creator: Chungen Liu 1 and Qiang Ren
description: Abstract . We consider the multi-bump solutions of the following fractional Nirenberg problem ( − Δ ) s ​ u = K ⁡ ( x ) ​ u n + 2 ​ s n − 2 ​ s , u > 0 ​ in ​ ℝ n , (-\Delta)^{s}u=K(x)u^{\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}},\;\;\;\;u>0\;\;\text{ in }\mathbb{R}^{n}, (0.

title: Fubini theorem in noncommutative geometry Note: Research supported by the ARC.
creator: F. Sukochev, D. Zanin
description: Abstract We discuss the Fubini formula in Alain Connes’ noncommutative geometry. We present a sufficient condition on spectral triples for which a Fubini formula holds true. The condition is natural and related to heat semigroup asymptotics. We provide examples of spectral triples for which the Fubini formula fails. 1 Introduction Fix throughout a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space H.

title: Minimal P P -symmetric period problem of first-order autonomous Hamiltonian Systems
creator: Chungen Liu, Ben-Xing Zhou
description: Abstract 1 1 footnotetext: Partially supported by the NSF of China (11471170, 10621101), 973 Program of MOST (2011CB808002) and SRFDP. Email: liucg@nankai.edu.cn (for Liu) and 1120130022@mail.nankai.edu.cn (for Zhou) Abstract : Let P\in Sp(2n) satisfying P^{k}=I_{2n} , we consider the minimal P -symmetric period problem of the autonomous nonlinear Hamiltonian system \dot{x}(t)=JH^{\prime}(x(t)).

title: Calculations of kaonic nuclei based on chiral meson-baryon coupled channel interaction models
creator: J. Hrtánková \fnsep, A. Cieplý, J. Mareš
description: Abstract We present our latest calculations of K − K^{-} -nuclear quasi-bound states using a self-consistent scheme for constructing K − K^{-} -nuclear potentials from various subthreshold chirally inspired K ¯ ​ N \bar{K}N scattering amplitudes. We consider in-medium versions of the scattering amplitudes taking into account Pauli blocking in the intermediate states.

title: The hierarchical generalized linear model and the bootstrap estimator of the error of prediction of loss reserves in a non-life insurance company
creator: Alicja Wolny-Dominiak
description: Abstract This paper presents the hierarchical generalized linear model (HGLM) for loss reserving in a non-life insurance company. Because in this case the error of prediction is expressed by a complex analytical formula, the error bootstrap estimator is proposed instead.

title: Subharmonic Solutions and Minimal Periodic Solutions of First-order Hamiltonian Systems with Anisotropic Growth
creator: Chungen Liu, Xiaofei Zhang
description: Abstract Abstract : Using a homologically link theorem in variational theory and iteration inequalities of Maslov-type index, we show the existence of a sequence of subharmonic solutions of non-autonomous Hamiltonian systems with the Hamiltonian functions satisfying some anisotropic growth conditions, i.e. , the Hamiltonian functions may have simultaneously, in different components, superquadratic, subquadratic and quadratic behaviors.

title: An estimate of Alpha decay half-life from the poles of S-matrix of an exactly solvable potential
creator: Swagatika Bhoi, Basudeb Sahu*
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Swagatika Bhoi, Basudeb Sahu*. We develop a versatile and analytically solvable potential which fairly reproduces the combined potential of an α + \alpha+ nucleus system resulting from both the attractive nuclear and repulsive electrostatic potentials. The potential is expressed in terms of the radial position, mass and proton number of the α \alpha -particle and the daughter nucleus and certain parameters governing the depth, height and steepness of the barrier.

title: A microscopically derived formula for alpha-decay half-lives
creator: Swagatika Bhoi, Basudeb Sahu*
description: Abstract Although Geiger-Nuttall (GN) law gives a single straight line, if we consider the experimental data of alpha particle emitters including heavy and super heavy nuclei with proton numbers as large as 118, instead of getting a single linear path we observe several linear segments with different slopes and intercepts.

title: Existence results for the fractional Q-curvature problem on three dimensional CR sphere Thanks: The first author is partially supported by the NSF of China (11471170, 10621101), 973 Program of MOST (2011CB808002) and SRFDP
creator: Chungen Liu, Yafang Wang
description: Abstract . In this paper the fractional Q-curvature problem on three dimensional CR sphere is considered. By using the critical points theory at infinity, an existence result is obtained. 1. Introduction and main result The sphere \mathbb{S}^{2n+1} is the boundary of the unit ball of \mathbb{C}^{n+1} . It is a contact manifold with a standard contact form \theta_{1} .

title: Combined Tractability of Query Evaluation via Tree Automata and Cycluits (Extended Version)
creator: Antoine Amarilli, Pierre Bourhis, Mikaël Monet, Pierre Senellart
description: Abstract We investigate parameterizations of both database instances and queries that make query evaluation fixed-parameter tractable in combined complexity. We introduce a new Datalog fragment with stratified negation, intensional-clique-guarded Datalog (ICG-Datalog), with linear-time evaluation on structures of bounded treewidth for programs of bounded rule size.

title: Stable rationality of higher dimensional conic bundles
creator: Hamid Ahmadinezhad, Takuzo Okada
description: Abstract We prove that a very general nonsingular conic bundle X → P n − 1 X\to\mathbb{P}^{n-1} embedded in a projective vector bundle of rank 3 3 over P n − 1 \mathbb{P}^{n-1} is not stably rational if the anti-canonical divisor of X X is not ample and n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 . Keywords.

title: Elliptic boundary-value problems in Hörmander spaces
creator: Anna Anop, Tetiana Kasirenko
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Anna Anop, Tetiana Kasirenko. We investigate general elliptic boundary-value problems in Hörmander inner product spaces that form the extended Sobolev scale. The latter consists of all Hilbert spaces that are interpolation spaces with respect to the Sobolev Hilbert scale. We prove that the operator corresponding to an arbitrary elliptic problem is Fredholm in appropriate couples of the Hörmander spaces and induces a collection of isomorphisms on the extended Sobolev scale.

title: TF.Learn: TensorFlow’s High-level Module for Distributed Machine Learning
creator: Yuan Tang terry.tang@uptake.com
description: Abstract TF.Learn is a high-level Python module for distributed machine learning inside TensorFlow ( Abadi et al. 2015 ) . It provides an easy-to-use Scikit-learn ( Pedregosa et al. 2011 ) style interface to simplify the process of creating, configuring, training, evaluating, and experimenting a machine learning model. TF.

title: Pseudo-magnetic field in curved graphene
creator: Pavel Castro-Villarreal, R. Ruiz-Sánchez
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Pavel Castro-Villarreal, R. Ruiz-Sánchez. The general covariance of the Dirac equation is exploited in order to explore the curvature effects appearing in the electronic properties of graphene. Two physical situations are then considered: the weak curvature regime, with | R | < 1 / L 2 \left|R\right|<1/L^{2} , and the strong curvature regime, with 1 / L 2 ≪ | R | < 1 / d 2 1/L^{2}\ll\left|R\right|<1/d^{2} , where R R is the scalar curvature, L L is a typical size of a

title: Stochastic laser cooling enabled by many body effects
creator: Roie Dann and Ronnie Kosloff
description: Abstract A novel laser cooling mechanism based on many body effects is presented. The method can be applicable for cooling a large class of atoms and molecules in higher density than commonly excepted by existing methods. The cooling mechanism relies on the collective encounters of particle and light.

title: Millimeter Wave Communications with OAM-SM Scheme for Future Mobile Networks
creator: Xiaohu Ge, Ran Zi, Xusheng Xiong, Qiang Li, Liang Wang, School of Electronic Information and Communications Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, Hubei, P. R. China. Email: {xhge, ranzi_pds, xiongxusheng, qli_patrick, M201671825}@mail.hust.edu.cn
description: Abstract The orbital angular momentum (OAM) technique provides a new degree of freedom for information transmissions in millimeter wave communications. Considering the spatial distribution characteristics of OAM beams, a new OAM spatial modulation (OAM-SM) millimeter wave communication system is first proposed for future mobile networks.

title: A positive characterization of rational maps
creator: Dylan P. Thurston
description: Abstract . When is a topological branched self-cover of the sphere equivalent to a post-critically finite rational map on ℂ ​ ℙ 1 \mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{1} ? William Thurston gave one answer in 1982, giving a negative criterion (an obstruction to a map being rational).

title: A Dual-Directional Path-loss Model in 5G Wireless Fractal Small Cell Networks This paper has submitted to IEEE ICC 2017.
creator: Jiaqi Chen 1 , Fen Bin 1 , Xiaohu Ge 1 , Qiang Li 1 , Cheng-Xiang Wang 2
description: Abstract With the anticipated increase in the number of low power base stations (BSs) deployed in small cell networks, blockage effects becoming more sensitive on wireless transmissions over high spectrums, variable propagation fading scenarios make it hard to describe coverage of small cell networks.

title: Johnson-Schechtman inequalities for noncommutative martingales Thanks: Yong Jiao is supported by NSFC(11471337) and Hunan Province NSF(14JJ1004).
creator: Yong Jiao, Fedor Sukochev, Dmitriy Zanin, Dejian Zhou
description: Abstract . In this paper we study Johnson-Schechtman inequalities for noncommutative martingales. More precisely, disjointification inequalities of noncommutative martingale difference sequences are proved in an arbitrary symmetric operator space E ⁡ ( ℳ ) E(\mathcal{M}) of a finite von Neumann algebra ℳ \mathcal{M} without making any assumption on the Boyd indices of E E .

title: Your Processor Leaks Information – and There’s Nothing You Can Do About It
creator: Qian Ge, Yuval Yarom, Frank Li, Gernot Heiser
description: Abstract Abstract Timing channels are information flows, encoded in the relative timing of events, that bypass the system’s protection mechanisms. Any microarchitectural state that depends on execution history and affects the rate of progress of later executions potentially establishes a timing channel, unless explicit steps are taken to close it.

title: Smart Contract Templates: essential requirements and design options
creator: Christopher D. Clack Centre for Blockchain Technologies Department of Computer Science University College London and Vikram A. Bakshi Investment Bank CTO Office Barclays and Lee Braine Investment Bank CTO Office Barclays
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Christopher D. Clack Centre for Blockchain Technologies Department of Computer Science University College London and Vikram A. Bakshi Investment Bank CTO Office Barclays and Lee Braine Investment Bank CTO Office Barclays. Smart Contract Templates support legally-enforceable smart contracts, using operational parameters to connect legal agreements to standardised code. In this paper, we explore the design landscape of potential formats for storage and transmission of smart legal agreements.

title: Cost Efficiency Optimization of 5G Wireless Backhaul Networks
creator: Xiaohu Ge, Song Tu, Guoqiang Mao, Vincent K. N. Lau, Linghui Pan, School of Electronic Information and Communications Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan 430074, Hubei, P. R. China. Email: {xhge, songtu, lhpan}@mail.hust.edu.cn School of Computing and Communications The University o
description: Abstract The wireless backhaul network provides an attractive solution for the urban deployment of fifth generation (5G) wireless networks that enables future ultra dense small cell networks to meet the ever-increasing user demands. Optimal deployment and management of 5G wireless backhaul networks is an interesting and challenging issue.

title: Banach limits and traces on ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} . Journal: Advances in Mathematics
creator: Evgeniy Semenov, Fedor Sukochev, Alexandr Usachev, Dmitriy Zanin
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Evgeniy Semenov, Fedor Sukochev, Alexandr Usachev, Dmitriy Zanin. We introduce a new approach to traces on the principal ideal ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} generated by any positive compact operator whose singular value sequence is the harmonic sequence. Distinct from the well-known construction of J. Dixmier, the new approach provides the explicit construction of every trace of every operator in ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} in terms of translation invariant functionals applied to a sequence of restricted sums of eigenvalues.

title: Singular traces and perturbation formulae of higher order Journal: Journal of Functional Analysis
creator: Denis Potapov, Fedor Sukochev, Alexandr Usachev, Dmitriy Zanin
description: Abstract Let H , V H,V be self-adjoint operators such that V V belongs to the weak trace class ideal. We prove higher order perturbation formula τ ⁡ ( f ⁡ ( H + V ) − ∑ j = 0 n − 1 1 j !

title: CHIPS Event Reconstruction and Design Optimisation
creator: A. Blake, S. Germani, Y. B. Pan, A. J. Perch, M. M. Pfützner, J. Thomas, L. H. Whitehead
description: Abstract The CHIPS experiment will comprise a 10 10\, kton water Cherenkov detector in an open mine pit in northern Minnesota, USA. The detector has been simulated using a full GEANT4 simulation and a series of event reconstruction algorithms have been developed to exploit the charge and time information from all of the PMTs.

title: Doran–Harder–Thompson Conjecture via SYZ Mirror Symmetry: Elliptic Curves This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Modular Forms and String Theory in honor of Noriko Yui. The full collection is available at http://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/modular-forms.html
creator: Atsushi KANAZAWA
description: Abstract We prove the Doran–Harder–Thompson conjecture in the case of elliptic curves by using ideas from SYZ mirror symmetry. The conjecture claims that when a Calabi–Yau manifold X X degenerates to a union of two quasi-Fano manifolds (Tyurin degeneration), a mirror Calabi–Yau manifold of X X can be constructed by gluing the two mirror Landau–Ginzburg models of the quasi-Fano manifolds.

title: Blind Measurement Selection: A Random Matrix Theory Approach
creator: Khalil Elkhalil, Abla Kammoun, Tareq Y. Al-Naffouri, Mohamed-Slim Alouini
description: Abstract This paper considers the problem of selecting a set of k k measurements from n n available sensor observations. The selected measurements should minimize a certain error function assessing the error in estimating a certain m m dimensional parameter vector.

title: The surface code with a twist
creator: Theodore J. Yoder, Isaac H. Kim
description: Abstract The surface code is one of the most successful approaches to topological quantum error-correction. It boasts the smallest known syndrome extraction circuits and correspondingly largest thresholds. Defect-based logical encodings of a new variety called twists have made it possible to implement the full Clifford group without state distillation. Here we investigate a patch-based encoding involving a modified twist.

title: On well-posedness of Ericksen-Leslie’s parabolic-hyperbolic liquid crystal model Thanks: August 7, 2026
creator: Ning Jiang, Yilong Luo
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Ning Jiang, Yilong Luo. We establish the following well-posedness results on Ericksen-Leslie’s parabolic-hyperbolic liquid crystal model: 1, if the dissipation coefficients β = μ 4 − 4 ​ μ 6 > 0 \beta=\mu_{4}-4\mu_{6}>0 , and the size of the initial energy E i ​ n E^{in} is small enough, then the life span of the solution is at least − O ⁡ ( ln ⁡ E i ​ n ) -O(\ln E^{in}) ; 2, for the special case that the coefficients μ 1 =

title: Optimal Quantum Metrology of Distant Black Bodies
creator: Mark E. Pearce, Earl T. Campbell, Pieter Kok
description: Abstract Measurements of an object’s temperature are important in many disciplines, from astronomy to engineering, as are estimates of an object’s spatial configuration. We present the quantum optimal estimator for the temperature of a distant body based on the black body radiation received in the far-field.

title: Electronic correlation effects and Coulomb gap in the Si(111)- ( 3 × 3 ) (\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}) -Sn surface
creator: A.B. Odobescu, A.A. Maizlakh, N.I. Fedotov, S.V. Zaitsev-Zotov
description: Abstract Electronic transport properties of the Si(111)- ( 3 × 3 ) (\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}) -Sn surface formed on low doped Si substrates are studied using two-probe conductivity measurements and tunnelling spectroscopy. We demonstrate that the ground state corresponds to Mott-Hubbard insulator with a band gap 2 ​ Δ = 70 2\Delta=70 meV, which vanishes quickly upon temperature increase.

title: Plasmons at the LaAlO 3 /SrTiO 3 interface and in the graphene-LaAlO 3 /SrTiO 3 double layer
creator: A. Faridi, Reza Asgari
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by A. Faridi, Reza Asgari. We study plasmon modes of the two-dimensional electron gas residing at the interface of band insulators LaAlO 3 \rm{LaAlO_{3}} and SrTiO 3 \rm{SrTiO_{3}} (LAO/STO) and the plasmon excitations of graphene-LAO/STO double layer as well. Considering the electron-electron interaction within random phase approximation, we calculate the plasmon dispersions of both systems numerically and in the long wavelength limit analytical expressions for collective modes are found.

title: Distributed algorithms for solving a class of convex feasibility problems
creator: Kaihong Lu, Gangshan Jing, and Long Wang
description: Abstract In this paper, a class of convex feasibility problems (CFPs) are studied for multi-agent systems through local interactions. The objective is to search a feasible solution to the convex inequalities with some set constraints in a distributed manner. The distributed control algorithms, involving subgradient and projection, are proposed for both continuous- and discrete-time systems, respectively.

title: Virtual Breathalyzer
creator: Ben Nassi , Lior Rokach, Yuval Elovici
description: Abstract Driving under the influence of alcohol is a widespread phenomenon in the US where it is considered a major cause of fatal accidents. In this research we present a novel approach and concept for detecting intoxication from motion differences obtained by the sensors of wearable devices.

title: A Multilinear Tongue Model Derived from Speech Related MRI Data of the Human Vocal Tract
creator: Alexander Hewer, Stefanie Wuhrer, Ingmar Steiner, Korin Richmond
description: Abstract We present a multilinear statistical model of the human tongue that captures anatomical and tongue pose related shape variations separately. The model is derived from 3D magnetic resonance imaging data of 11 speakers sustaining speech related vocal tract configurations.

title: Feature Learning for Chord Recognition: The Deep Chroma Extractor
description: Abstract We explore frame-level audio feature learning for chord recognition using artificial neural networks. We present the argument that chroma vectors potentially hold enough information to model harmonic content of audio for chord recognition, but that standard chroma extractors compute too noisy features. This leads us to propose a learned chroma feature extractor based on artificial neural networks.

title: Measurement of C ​ P C\!P asymmetries in D 0 → h ​ h D^{0}\rightarrow hh decays
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by . The latest measurements of the individual time-integrated C ​ P C\!P asymmetry in the Cabibbo-suppressed decays D 0 → h ​ h {{D}^{0}}\rightarrow hh decays are presented. The results are based on p ​ p pp collision data, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 3 fb − 1 \mbox{\,fb}^{-1} , collected with the LHCb detector at centre-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 Te ​ V \mathrm{\,Te\kern-1.00006ptV} .

title: Theory and Phenomenology of Composite 2-Higgs Doublet Models
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by . In this talk, we report unitarity constraints and phenomenological studies at the Large Hadron Collider for the extra Higgs bosons of a Composite 2-Higgs Doublet Model. † † conference: Prospects for Charged Higgs Discovery at Colliders 3-6 October 2016 Uppsala, Sweden 1 Introduction After the discovery of a Higgs like state at the mass of 125 GeV at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in July 2012 [ 1 , 2 ] , understanding the origin of Electro-Weak Symmetry Breaking (EWSB) is one of

title: Categorial Independence and Lévy Processes This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Non-Commutative Algebra, Probability and Analysis in Action. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/non-commutative-probability.html
creator: Malte GERHOLD ab, Stephanie LACHS a and Michael SCHÜRMANN a
description: Abstract We generalize Franz’ independence in tensor categories with inclusions from two morphisms (which represent generalized random variables) to arbitrary ordered families of morphisms. We will see that this only works consistently if the unit object is an initial object, in which case the inclusions can be defined starting from the tensor category alone.

title: On the Potential of Simple Framewise Approaches to Piano Transcription
description: Abstract In an attempt at exploring the limitations of simple approaches to the task of piano transcription (as usually defined in MIR), we conduct an in-depth analysis of neural network-based framewise transcription. We systematically compare different popular input representations for transcription systems to determine the ones most suitable for use with neural networks.

title: Covalency and vibronic couplings make a nonmagnetic j = 3 / 2 j\!=\!3/2 ion magnetic
creator: Lei Xu, Nikolay A. Bogdanov, Andrew Princep, Peter Fulde, Jeroen van den Brink, Liviu Hozoi
description: Abstract ABSTRACT For 4 d 1 d^{1} and 5 d 1 d^{1} spin-orbit-coupled electron configurations, the notion of nonmagnetic j = 3 / 2 j\!=\!3/2 quartet ground state discussed in classical textbooks is at odds with the observed variety of magnetic properties.

title: The CENDARI Infrastructure
creator: Nadia Boukhelifa Mike Bryant Nataša Bulatović Ivan Čukić Jean-Daniel Fekete Milica Knežević Jörg Lehmann David Stuart Carsten Thiel
description: Abstract The CENDARI infrastructure is a research supporting platform designed to provide tools for transnational historical research, focusing on two topics : Medieval culture and World War I . It exposes to the end users modern web-based tools relying on a sophisticated infrastructure to collect, enrich, annotate, and search through large document corpora.

title: Fast, Dense Feature SDM on an iPhone
creator: Ashton Fagg, Simon Lucey, Sridha Sridharan Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA
description: Abstract In this paper, we present our method for enabling dense SDM to run at over 90 FPS on a mobile device. Our contributions are two-fold. Drawing inspiration from the FFT, we propose a Sparse Compositional Regression (SCR) framework, which enables a significant speed up over classical dense regressors. Second, we propose a binary approximation to SIFT features.

title: Medical Image Synthesis with Context-Aware Generative Adversarial Networks
creator: Dong Nie, Roger Trullo, Caroline Petitjean, Su Ruan, Dinggang Shen
description: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) is critical for various clinical applications, e.g., radiotherapy treatment planning and also PET attenuation correction. However, CT exposes radiation during acquisition, which may cause side effects to patients. Compared to CT, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is much safer and does not involve any radiations.

title: A Two-Phase Approach Towards Identifying Argument Structure in Natural Language
creator: Arkanath Pathak, Pawan Goyal, Plaban Bhowmick
description: Abstract We propose a new approach for extracting argument structure from natural language texts that contain an underlying argument. Our approach comprises of two phases: Score Assignment and Structure Prediction. The Score Assignment phase trains models to classify relations between argument units (Support, Attack or Neutral). To that end, different training strategies have been explored.

title: From Multisets to Sets in Homotopy Type Theory
creator: Håkon Robbestad Gylterud
description: Abstract We give a model of set theory based on multisets in homotopy type theory. The equality of the model is the identity type. The underlying type of iterative sets can be formulated in Martin-Löf type theory, without Higher Inductive Types (HITs), and is a sub-type of the underlying type of Aczel’s 1978 model of set theory in type theory.

title: On-bird Sound Recordings: Automatic Acoustic Recognition of Activities and Contexts
creator: Dan Stowell, Emmanouil Benetos, Lisa F. Gill
description: Abstract We introduce a novel approach to studying animal behaviour and the context in which it occurs, through the use of microphone backpacks carried on the backs of individual free-flying birds. These sensors are increasingly used by animal behaviour researchers to study individual vocalisations of freely behaving animals, even in the field.

title: On the crucial impact of the coupling projector-backprojector in iterative tomographic reconstruction
creator: Filippo Arcadu, Marco Stampanoni, Federica Marone, [1ex] Institute for Biomedical Engineering, ETH Zurich, 8092 Zurich, Switzerland

title: Factor Ordering and Path Integral Measure for Quantum Gravity in (1+1) Dimensions
creator: John HAGA and Rachel Lash MAITRA
description: Abstract We develop a mathematically rigorous path integral representation of the time evolution operator for a model of (1+1) quantum gravity that incorporates factor ordering ambiguity. In obtaining a suitable integral kernel for the time-evolution operator, one requires that the corresponding Hamiltonian is self-adjoint; this issue is subtle for a particular category of factor orderings.

title: Loop Models and 𝑲 \boldsymbol{K} -Theory This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Combinatorics of Moduli Spaces: Integrability, Cohomology, Quantisation, and Beyond. The full collection is available at http://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/moduli-spaces-2016.html
creator: Paul ZINN-JUSTIN
description: Abstract This is a review/announcement of results concerning the connection between certain exactly solvable two-dimensional models of statistical mechanics, namely loop models, and the equivariant K K -theory of the cotangent bundle of the Grassmannian. We interpret various concepts from integrable systems ( R R -matrix, partition function on a finite domain) in geometric terms.

title: PARSEC-SCALE STRUCTURE AND KINEMATICS OF FAINT TEV HBLS
creator: B. Glenn Piner, Philip G. Edwards
description: Abstract We present new multi-epoch Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) observations of a set of TeV blazars drawn from our VLBA program to monitor all TeV-detected high-frequency peaked BL Lac objects (HBLs) at parsec scales. Most of these sources are faint in the radio, so they have not been well observed with VLBI by other surveys.

title: Dust Scattering from the Taurus Molecular Cloud Dust Scattering from the Taurus Molecular Cloud – References 2015
creator: Sathyanarayan, Jayant Murthy, K. Narayanankutty
description: Abstract We present an analysis of the diffuse ultraviolet (UV) emission near the Taurus Molecular Cloud based on observations made by the Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX). We used a Monte Carlo dust scattering model to show that about half of the scattered flux originates in the molecular cloud with 25% arising in the foreground and 25% behind the cloud.

title: 3d steady Gradient Ricci Solitons with linear curvature decay Thanks: * Partially supported by the NSFC Grants 11271022 and 11331001
creator: Yuxing Deng, Xiaohua Zhu ∗ \text{Zhu}^{*}
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Yuxing Deng, Xiaohua Zhu ∗ \text{Zhu}^{*}. In this note, we prove that a 3-dimensional steady Ricci soliton is rotationally symmetric if its scalar curvature R ⁡ ( x ) R(x) satisfies C 0 − 1 ρ ⁡ ( x ) ≤ R ⁡ ( x ) ≤ C 0 ρ ⁡ ( x ) \frac{C_{0}^{-1}}{\rho(x)}\leq R(x)\leq\frac{C_{0}}{\rho(x)} for some constant C 0 > 0 C_{0}>0 , where ρ ⁡ ( x ) \rho(x) denotes the distance from a fixed point x 0 x_{0} .

title: Learning a No-Reference Quality Metric for Single-Image Super-Resolution Journal: Computer Vision and Image Understanding
creator: Chao Ma, Chih-Yuan Yang, Xiaokang Yang, Ming-Hsuan Yang
description: Abstract Numerous single-image super-resolution algorithms have been proposed in the literature, but few studies address the problem of performance evaluation based on visual perception. While most super-resolution images are evaluated by full-reference metrics, the effectiveness is not clear and the required ground-truth images are not always available in practice.

title: Implementations and the independent set polynomial below the Shearer threshold Thanks: To appear in Theoretical Computer Science . A preliminary short version of this paper (without the proofs) appeared in the Proceedings of ICALP 2017 [ 3 ] .
creator: Andreas Galanis, Leslie Ann GoldbergDaniel Štefankovič
description: Abstract The independent set polynomial is important in many areas of combinatorics, computer science, and statistical physics. For every integer Δ ≥ 2 \Delta\geq 2 , the Shearer threshold is the value λ ∗ ​ ( Δ ) = ( Δ − 1 ) Δ − 1 / Δ Δ \lambda^{*}(\Delta)=(\Delta-1)^{\Delta-1}/\Delta^{\Delta} .

title: The Giry Monad is not Strong for the Canonical Symmetric Monoidal Closed Structure on 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐬 \mathbf{Meas}
creator: Tetsuya Sato
description: Abstract We show that the Giry monad is not strong with respect to the canonical symmetric monoidal closed structure on the category 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐬 \mathbf{Meas} of all measurable spaces and measurable functions. 1 Introduction A motivation of this research is to give a denotational semantics of Higher-order continuous probabilistic programming language.

title: Reconstruction of Refractive Indices from Spectral Measurements of Monodisperse Aerosols
creator: Tobias Kyrion
description: Abstract For the investigation of two-component aerosols one needs to know the refractive indices of the two aerosol components. One problem is that they depend on temparature and pressure, so one needs for their determination a robust measurement instrument such as the FASP device, which can cope with rigid environmental conditions.

title: An empirical and theoretical critique of the Euclidean Index Journal: Journal of Informetrics
creator: Jens Peter Andersen
description: Abstract The recently proposed Euclidean index offers a novel approach to measure the citation impact of academic authors, in particular as an alternative to the h h -index. We test if the index provides new, robust information, not covered by existing bibliometric indicators, discuss the measurement scale and the degree of distinction between analytical units the index offers.

title: Handwritten Signature Verification Using Hand-Worn Devices
creator: Ben Nassi 1 , Alona Levy 2 , Yuval Elovici 1 Erez Shmueli 2
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Ben Nassi 1 , Alona Levy 2 , Yuval Elovici 1 Erez Shmueli 2. Online signature verification technologies, such as those available in banks and post offices, rely on dedicated digital devices such as tablets or smart pens to capture, analyze and verify signatures. In this paper, we suggest a novel method for online signature verification that relies on the increasingly available hand-worn devices, such as smartwatches or fitness trackers, instead of dedicated ad-hoc devices.

title: A Minimal Model of Burst-Noise Induced Bistability
creator: Johannes Falk, Marc Mendler, Barbara Drossel
description: Abstract We investigate the influence of intrinsic noise on stable states of a one-dimensional dynamical system that shows in its deterministic version a saddle-node bifurcation between monostable and bistable behaviour. The system is a modified version of the Schlögl model, which is a chemical reaction system with only one type of molecule.

title: Projection effects in the strong lensing study of subhaloes
creator: Ran Li, Carlos S. Frenk, Shaun Cole, Qiao Wang, Liang Gao
description: Abstract The defining characteristic of the cold dark matter (CDM) hypothesis is the presence of a very large number of low-mass haloes, too small to have made a visible galaxy. Other hypotheses for the nature of the dark matter, such as warm dark matter (WDM), predict a much smaller number of such low-mass haloes.

title: On electrodynamics of chiral matter
creator: Zebin Qiu, Gaoqing Cao, Xu-Guang Huang
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Zebin Qiu, Gaoqing Cao, Xu-Guang Huang. Many-body systems with chiral fermions can exhibit novel transport phenomena that violate parity and time reversal symmetries, such as the chiral magnetic effect, the anomalous Hall effect, and the anomalous generation of charge. Based on the Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics, we examine some electromagnetic and optical properties of such systems including the electrostatics, the magnetostatics, the propagation of electromagnetic waves, the novel optical effects, etc.

title: On the influence of a Hybrid Thermal-Non thermal distribution in the Internal Shocks model for blazars
creator: J. M. Rueda-Becerril, P. Mimica, M.A. Aloy
description: Abstract Internal shocks occurring in blazars may accelerate both thermal and non-thermal electrons. In this paper we examine the consequences that such a hybrid (thermal/non-thermal) EED has on the spectrum of blazars. Since the thermal component of the EED may extend to very low energies. We replace the standard synchrotron process by the more general magneto-bremsstrahlung (MBS).

title: The Impact of the Filter Bubble—A Simulation Based Framework for Measuring Personalisation Macro Effects in Online Communities
creator: Thomas Gottron Felix Schwagereit
description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Thomas Gottron Felix Schwagereit. The term filter bubble has been coined to describe the situation of online users which—due to filtering algorithms—live in a personalised information universe biased towards their own interests. In this paper we use an agent-based simulation framework to measure the actual risk and impact of filter bubble effects occurring in online communities due to content or author based personalisation algorithms. Observing the strength of filter bubble effects allows for opposing the benefits to the risks of personalisation.
